genericAnswers.value: All change-request artifacts for the release under design assurance: architecture diagrams (C4 model in Confluence space ARCH), pull requests and code-review records in GitHub Enterprise repo, CI test results from the Jenkins pipeline, and the risk log in the GRC platform. Scope = one release train / one Jira epic (e.g. EPIC-1420).
The current release cycle only: from feature-branch cut to release-candidate freeze (e.g. 2026-06-15 through 2026-06-30); evidence dated outside this window is excluded.

Each evidence item carries: source URL/permalink, author, timestamp, and Jira issue key. Architecture diagram version tag present; code-review record shows 2 approvers; test-result artifact shows pass rate and coverage %. Any field blank = item rejected.

Evidence item count reconciles to the assurance checklist: 1 architecture diagram + N code-review records (= N merged PRs in the epic) + 1 CI test-result set + 1 risk-log export. Delta must be 0; any missing item logged as a gap.

All collected evidence uploaded to the compliance evidence repository under folder /assurance/<epic-key>/ with immutable timestamp and version label v<n>; retention 3 years per NYDFS audit-trail requirement.

Missing or stale evidence raised as Jira issue type 'SDLC-Exception', assignee = Engineering Manager, disposition (waiver / remediate / accept-risk) recorded with reason and 10-business-day remediation SLA.

Pre/post comparison: assurance-evidence bundle diffed against the prior release bundle to confirm all mandatory artifact types present and no regressions in coverage or open-risk count; comparison report attached to the change ticket.
Change ticket = ServiceNow CHG record for the release, cross-linked to the Jira epic and the GitHub release tag; ticket URL recorded on the evidence bundle cover sheet.
100% of mandatory assurance artifacts for the epic (architecture diagram, all code-review records, CI results, risk log) — no sampling; census test of the full evidence set.
PASS = all 4 mandatory artifact types present, each with valid version/timestamp and required approvals; 0 items missing. FAIL = any mandatory artifact absent, unversioned, or lacking sign-off.

On FAIL, block the assurance gate, open an 'SDLC-Exception' Jira ticket (owner = Engineering Manager), and either obtain the missing artifact or record an approved waiver before release; 10-business-day remediation SLA.
Field definitions sourced from the assurance-checklist data dictionary in Confluence: artifact_type, source_url, author, timestamp, jira_key, version, approver_count — one row per evidence item.

Control total = expected artifact count derived from Jira (merged-PR count + fixed set of 3 non-PR artifacts); reconciles against rows extracted from GitHub Enterprise and the CI system with 0 variance.
All open remediation items arising from design-assurance, code review, security scans and audit findings for the release, tracked as Jira issues labelled 'remediation' under the current epic.
Current remediation cycle: from finding creation date to target closure date within the release window (e.g. 2026-06-01 to 2026-07-15).
Each remediation Jira item has: severity, owner, root cause, linked finding, target date, and closure evidence link. Items missing owner or target date are flagged as invalid and returned to triage.
Open-item count in the GRC platform reconciles to the Jira remediation board; closed items must have a linked verification artifact. Delta between GRC and Jira must be 0 at close of cycle.
Closure evidence (retest result, merged fix PR, config screenshot) attached to each Jira item and exported to the compliance evidence repository with timestamp and version; retained 3 years.

Items that cannot close within SLA logged as 'SDLC-Exception' with disposition (risk-accept / extend / waive), owner = Engineering Manager, and documented rationale; 10-business-day extension SLA before re-escalation.
Pre/post comparison of the remediation board: open-item count at cycle start vs end; every item that moved to Closed has a verification artifact; 0 items closed without evidence.
Each remediation item links to its originating finding and, where a code change was required, to the ServiceNow CHG record and merged GitHub PR that delivered the fix.
100% of remediation items in the epic (census); no sampling — every open and recently-closed item is checked for valid closure.
PASS = all critical/high items closed with verification evidence; ≤5 medium items open only with an approved waiver. FAIL = any critical/high open past SLA, or any 'Closed' item lacking evidence.
On FAIL, block release sign-off; open 'SDLC-Exception' (owner = Engineering Manager) for each overdue item with remediation plan and 10-business-day SLA; escalate critical items to the ARB.
Effective dates = finding-open date through verified-closed date; only items with activity in the current release window are in scope for this closure test.
The streaming consumer(s) for the target Kafka topic(s) and their dead-letter topic(s); scope = one pipeline (e.g. policy-events consumer group) processing messages off Azure Event Hubs / Kafka.
Development and test window for the DLQ feature branch, e.g. 2026-06-20 to 2026-07-05, covering unit + integration test runs against a synthetic poison-message set.

Each DLQ record carries: original topic, partition, offset, failure reason, retry count, and first-seen timestamp. Records missing failure reason or offset are themselves alerted as a defect in the handler.
In test: (messages consumed) = (successfully processed) + (routed to DLQ); no message lost or double-counted. Reconciliation over a 10,000-message synthetic batch must balance exactly (delta = 0).

Test results (poison-message routing report, offset reconciliation) stored as CI artifacts in the pipeline run and archived to the source/CI-CD repository release folder with commit SHA and timestamp.

Messages exceeding max-retry (default 3) are routed to the DLQ with disposition metadata; DLQ backlog above threshold raises a monitoring alert and an 'SDLC-Exception' Jira item, owner = Engineering Manager.

Pre/post: replay the synthetic poison-message batch before and after the change; before = messages block/crash the consumer, after = bad messages land in DLQ and good messages continue; comparison report attached to PR.
Change ticket = ServiceNow CHG for the pipeline deployment, linked to the Jira story and the merged GitHub PR delivering the DLQ handler.
Synthetic test set of 10,000 messages including ≥500 crafted poison messages (malformed schema, null keys, oversized payloads) plus valid controls; run in the CI integration stage.
PASS = 100% of poison messages routed to DLQ with correct metadata, 0 valid messages dropped, 0 consumer crashes. FAIL = any poison message reprocessed indefinitely or any valid message lost.

Messages that still cannot be classified route to a secondary quarantine topic and page the on-call via PagerDuty; recurring poison patterns logged as an 'SDLC-Exception' for handler fix within 10 business days.
Test run effective date = CI pipeline run date for the feature branch; results valid for the RC built from that commit only.

The full functional regression suite plus new-feature test cases mapped to the release candidate's user stories; scope = all test cases tagged to the release epic in the test management tool (Xray/Zephyr in Jira).
The RC test window: from RC build date to go/no-go decision (e.g. 2026-06-28 to 2026-07-02); only executions against the frozen RC build are in scope.
Each executed test case records: build/version under test, tester, timestamp, status (pass/fail/blocked), and defect link on failure. Executions missing build id or status are re-run.
Executed count reconciles to planned count: (planned test cases) = (passed) + (failed) + (blocked) + (skipped-with-reason). No case left in 'not run' at go/no-go; delta = 0.

Test execution report and automated run logs (JUnit XML) exported from Jenkins/GitHub Actions and attached to the Xray test plan with RC version tag and timestamp; retained per release evidence policy.

Each failed test raises a linked defect (Jira Bug); blocked cases record blocker reason. Failures not fixed pre-release logged as 'SDLC-Exception' with risk disposition, owner = QA Lead, 10-business-day SLA.
100% of regression cases for changed components + all new-feature acceptance cases for the RC; risk-based full run, no sampling on critical paths.
PASS = 100% of critical/high-priority cases pass, ≥98% overall pass rate, 0 open critical/high defects. FAIL = any critical case fails or overall pass rate < 98%.
On failure, log a Jira Bug linked to the test case, triage severity, and gate release; unresolved criticals block go-live or require an approved 'SDLC-Exception' from the Release Manager.
Acceptance criteria = the Given/When/Then criteria on each linked user story; a story is 'tested' only when all its acceptance criteria have a passing test execution against the RC.
Evidence stored in the Xray/Zephyr test plan for the release epic (execution records + attached automated logs), URL recorded on the release go/no-go record in ServiceNow.

Engagement metrics for the engineering knowledge base (Confluence 'ENG' space + internal docs portal): page views, unique readers, search queries, and helpfulness ratings across all published runbooks, ADRs and how-to articles.
Rolling reporting period, most recent full quarter (e.g. Q2 2026, 2026-04-01 to 2026-06-30), with month-over-month trend.
Each metric row has: article id, period, views, unique_users, avg_rating, search_hits. Rows with null article id or period are excluded from the dashboard as invalid.

Sum of per-article views reconciles to the platform-level total pageview count for the period within ±1%; unique-user total reconciles to the SSO analytics feed. Larger variance triggers a data-quality check.
The engagement report (dashboard snapshot + underlying extract) saved to the BI platform with report version and refresh timestamp; extract archived to the data warehouse engagement schema.
Articles with 0 views or rating < 3 flagged for review; stale/low-value content raised as a Jira 'docs-review' item to the content owner with a 10-business-day triage window.
All published knowledge-base articles active in the reporting quarter (census), joined to the analytics event stream for that period.
PASS = engagement extract reconciles to source analytics within ±1% and dashboard refreshes on schedule. FAIL = reconciliation variance > 1% or a missing daily analytics load in the period.
On reconciliation failure, hold dashboard publication, open a data-quality Jira item to the Data Engineer, backfill the missing analytics load, and re-run; 10-business-day resolution SLA.

Delegation matrix documented in Confluence: metric definitions and dashboard changes approved by the Tech Lead; in their absence the delegate is the Engineering Manager; recorded in the report governance page.

The integration components for the initiative: API/middleware code, config, and connectors delivered into the target environment (e.g. Guidewire ClaimCenter ↔ payments API via Azure API Management); scope = one integration story/epic in Jira.
Build-and-deploy window for the integration release (e.g. sprint 2026-06-16 to 2026-06-27) through promotion to the target (test/prod) environment.
Deliverable metadata complete: repo + commit SHA, deployed environment, API contract (OpenAPI) version, and smoke-test result. Missing contract version or deploy target blocks promotion.
Deployed artifact version reconciles to the approved build in the CI/CD repository and to the change ticket; smoke-test transaction count in = out across the integration with 0 discrepancy.
Build artifact, deployment log, and post-deploy smoke-test report stored as pipeline artifacts and linked from the ServiceNow CHG record with version tag and timestamp.
Failed deployment or smoke test triggers automatic rollback to the prior version and an 'SDLC-Exception' Jira item, owner = DevOps Engineer, with root cause and 10-business-day fix SLA.

All API gateway and middleware components in production for the platform (Azure API Management instances, routing policies, rate limits, health probes); scope = the API estate owned by the integration team.
Current operational monitoring period (rolling 30 days), with incident/SLA review at each month close.
Each gateway config item has: route, upstream, policy set (auth, rate limit), and health-probe definition. Any route missing an auth policy or health probe is flagged non-compliant.
Deployed gateway routes reconcile to the source-controlled API config (IaC); count and policy hash in production match the repo. Drift (delta > 0) raises a config-drift alert.
Gateway config exported to source control on each change; monitoring dashboards and monthly SLA reports archived with timestamp; retained per operations evidence policy.

Health-check failures or SLA breaches open a ServiceNow incident and page on-call; recurring issues become problem records; unresolved policy drift logged as 'SDLC-Exception', owner = Platform Engineering Lead, 10-business-day SLA.
Backlog items slated for the upcoming planning increment that require effort sizing; scope = all 'Ready for estimation' stories in the team backlog in Jira for the next 1-2 sprints.
Current planning cycle: the estimation session(s) held before sprint/PI planning (e.g. the week of 2026-07-07).
Each estimated item has: story points, acceptance criteria, dependencies noted, and estimator consensus recorded. Items without acceptance criteria are returned to refinement, not estimated.
Count of estimated items reconciles to the 'Ready for estimation' queue; every in-scope item has a non-zero point value at session end; unestimated count must be 0.
Estimation results (points per story, planning-poker outcome) saved on each Jira item and in the sprint-planning Confluence page with date and participant list.

Items with wide estimate spread or unresolved dependencies flagged as 'needs-spike' and deferred with a note; exceptions to the Definition of Ready recorded for Product Owner decision within the sprint.
All backlog items in the 'Ready for estimation' state for the planning cycle (census).

PASS = 100% of in-scope items carry a point estimate and meet the Definition of Ready; no single story estimated above the team's split threshold (e.g. 13 points). FAIL = any in-scope item unestimated or oversized without a split/spike.
Oversized or ambiguous items are split or converted to a time-boxed spike; unresolved items excluded from the sprint and returned to backlog refinement with an owner and a target refinement date.

Definition of Ready = clear acceptance criteria, no blocking dependency, testable, and small enough to complete in a sprint; an item is estimable only when it meets the DoR documented in the team charter.
Estimates recorded on the Jira items and summarised on the sprint-planning Confluence page; link included in the sprint-planning meeting notes.

The elaborated scope package for the initiative: refined requirements, acceptance criteria, and impact analysis awaiting formal stakeholder sign-off; scope = one requirements baseline / one Jira epic.
The elaboration cycle up to the sign-off gate (e.g. 2026-06-10 to 2026-06-24); sign-off applies to this baseline version only.
Scope package complete: every requirement has an id, acceptance criteria, priority, and traceability to a business objective. Requirements missing acceptance criteria are not eligible for sign-off.
Requirement count in the sign-off package reconciles to the requirements register; each has exactly one approval status. Unapproved-but-in-scope count must be 0 at gate.
Signed-off scope baseline (with e-signature/approval record) versioned in Confluence and the requirements tool with timestamp; superseded versions retained for audit.

Requirements not approved are parked with rationale; scope changes after sign-off follow the change-control process and require re-approval; disagreements escalated per the RACI, owner = Product Owner, 10-business-day resolution.
The requirements elaboration method (e.g. BABOK-aligned analysis with traceability matrix) and its template version are approved and recorded on the baseline cover page.
Sensitivity: any requirement whose change would alter cost/schedule by > 10% or touch a regulated data flow is marked high-sensitivity and requires senior stakeholder approval.
Materiality: scope items below 2 story points and with no regulatory/data impact may be approved by the Product Owner alone; above that threshold require the full sign-off panel.
The go/hold decision, approver names, date, and any conditions recorded in the sign-off record in Confluence and linked on the Jira epic.
Communication recipients = Product Owner, Tech Lead, QA Lead, delivery team, and named business sponsor; distribution logged via the Confluence page watchers and a notification email retained.
All requirements in the sign-off baseline (census) plus their linked acceptance criteria and traceability entries.

PASS = 100% of in-scope requirements have acceptance criteria, traceability, and an approval status of 'Approved' from an authorised approver. FAIL = any requirement lacking criteria, traceability, or valid approval.

Requirements failing validation are returned to elaboration; the sign-off gate is not passed until all criticals are resolved or an approved exception is recorded by the Product Owner (10-business-day SLA).
Sign-off is effective for the named baseline version and its effective date; any later requirement change invalidates the sign-off for the affected items and requires re-approval.

The requirements for the streaming use case: latency, throughput, ordering/exactly-once guarantees, retention, and schema evolution for the target real-time pipeline (e.g. policy-change events on Kafka/Azure Event Hubs); scope = one streaming use-case epic.
Requirements definition phase for the use case (e.g. 2026-06-05 to 2026-06-19), ending at requirements agreement sign-off.

Each requirement has measurable targets: latency (e.g. p99 < 2s), throughput (events/sec), ordering guarantee (per-key), and delivery semantics (at-least-once/exactly-once). Requirements without a quantified target are not accepted.

Requirement set reconciles to the use-case template (latency, throughput, ordering, retention, schema, SLA all present); any missing NFR category flagged as a gap; missing-count must be 0 at agreement.
Agreed requirements document versioned in Confluence with sign-off date and stakeholder list; linked from the Jira epic; superseded versions retained.

Unresolved or conflicting NFRs (e.g. exactly-once vs latency trade-off) logged as open questions with an owner and target date; unagreed items block the epic and are escalated to the Product Owner, 10-business-day SLA.
All requirements in the streaming use-case baseline (census), including every NFR category and its acceptance criteria.
PASS = every requirement is specific, measurable and testable with a quantified target, and all stakeholders have agreed. FAIL = any requirement vague/unquantified or any NFR category missing.

Non-measurable requirements returned to the author for quantification; unresolved trade-offs decided by the architecture team and Product Owner; exceptions to completeness recorded with rationale before agreement.
Acceptance criteria per requirement stated as testable conditions (e.g. 'under 5k events/sec sustained load, p99 end-to-end latency < 2s over a 1-hour run'); each maps to a future test case.
Agreed requirements stored in the Confluence use-case space and referenced on the Jira epic; sign-off record links the exact document version.

All engineers joining the Software Engineering & Delivery org (target ~6-10 hires/quarter); scope = access provisioning, environment setup, and completion of the mandatory onboarding runbook checklist for each named hire.
First 30 days from the hire's start date; onboarding runbook must be signed off no later than day 30, with day-1/day-7/day-30 milestone gates tracked in the hire's ServiceNow onboarding case.

Each ServiceNow onboarding case must carry: hire name, start date, assigned Tech Lead/buddy, team, and the linked Confluence runbook version; provisioning tasks (repo access, CI/CD, IAM group) all in state Closed-Complete before the case can close.

Count of onboarding checklist items marked Complete equals total items in the runbook version (0 open items); repo/tooling access grants reconcile 1:1 to the role-based access template for the hire's title.
Retain the completed onboarding checklist as a PDF/record attached to the ServiceNow case with close timestamp and runbook version tag; retention 3 years per HR/audit policy.

Any incomplete item at day 30 logged as an exception on the ServiceNow case with owner = assigned Tech Lead and a remediation due date; escalate to Engineering Manager if open beyond 10 business days.
Compare the hire's granted access set post-provisioning against the role-based access baseline for their title; comparison must show 0 excess grants and 0 missing required grants before sign-off.
Every provisioning action links to the ServiceNow onboarding case number (format INC/RITM); no manual access grant permitted without a linked ticket.
Onboarding completion decision recorded in the ServiceNow case activity log by the Tech Lead, stating checklist complete and access verified against baseline.
Notify the hiring Engineering Manager, HR business partner, and team distribution list on case closure; recipients captured in the ServiceNow case watch-list.
Sample the last quarter's onboarding cases (or 100% if fewer than 20); verify each has a completed runbook and access reconciliation record.
Pass = every sampled case has checklist 100% complete, access reconciled to baseline, and sign-off captured; fail if any case is missing sign-off or shows unreconciled access.
Failed cases raised as ServiceNow exception tasks, owner = Engineering Manager, 10-business-day remediation SLA; access anomalies routed to IAM for immediate review.
Onboarding runbook version approved by the Platform Engineering Lead; current version tag recorded on the Confluence page and referenced in each case.
Role-based access baselines sourced from the IAM access template repository (Okta/SailPoint) keyed by job title; runbook content sourced from the team Confluence knowledge base.

Production streaming pipelines on the real-time platform (Kafka topics feeding the lakehouse) whose consumer lag or throughput breached SLA in the last 30 days; scope = partition counts, consumer parallelism, and back-pressure/rate-limit settings for those topics.
Tuning window covers the trailing 30 days of production telemetry; changes validated over a 7-day post-change observation period before closing the change.

Telemetry inputs must include per-topic consumer lag, records/sec throughput, end-to-end p99 latency, and error rate for the tuning window; each metric non-null and sourced from the observability platform dashboard for the target service.

Post-tune, sustained consumer lag returns to <= agreed SLA (e.g. p99 lag < 5s / < 10k messages) and throughput handles peak load with < 70% partition utilization; before/after metric deltas recorded in the change ticket.
Attach before/after dashboard snapshots and the applied config diff to the ServiceNow change ticket with timestamp and pipeline config version/commit SHA.
Any topic still breaching SLA after tuning logged as an exception on the change ticket with owner = Data Engineer and a follow-up capacity/design review scheduled within 5 business days.
The specific tuned topics/consumer groups (named), replayed under representative peak load in staging plus the 7-day production observation window.

Pass = p99 end-to-end latency and consumer lag within SLA under peak load with 0 dropped/duplicated records (idempotent replay verified); fail if lag grows unbounded or back-pressure causes upstream producer errors.
On fail, revert to the previous config version (stored in the CI/CD repo) via instant rollback and reopen the tuning task; escalate persistent SLA breach to Platform Engineering Lead.
Acceptance: sustained SLA compliance over the 7-day window (0 SLA-breach alerts), throughput headroom >= 30%, and no increase in downstream error rate vs. baseline.
Config diff and commit in the source/CI-CD repo; before/after telemetry and load-test results attached to the ServiceNow change ticket and linked from the service runbook.
All approved business requirements for the current epic/feature in Jira; scope = decomposition into user stories with INVEST-compliant acceptance criteria for each in-scope requirement.
Current PI/sprint planning cycle; stories drafted and ready no later than 2 business days before the sprint-planning session that will pull them.

Each Jira story must have: title in user-story form, description, acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then), link to parent requirement/epic, and value stream/component label populated before it leaves Draft.
Count of drafted stories maps to 100% of in-scope requirements (traceability matrix shows every requirement covered by >=1 story; 0 orphan requirements).
Traceability matrix and story set exported/linked in Confluence with timestamp and epic version; Jira retains full change history on each story.

Requirements that cannot be storified (ambiguous/blocked) logged as an exception in the epic with owner = Business Analyst and a clarification due date; escalate to Product Owner if open beyond 5 business days.
Story-writing follows the team's approved requirements-elaboration standard (INVEST + Given/When/Then AC template), version referenced on the epic.
Stories exceeding the team's story-point ceiling (e.g. > 8 points) must be split; splitting threshold documented in the team working agreement.
Requirements below the minimum-value threshold (no user/business outcome) are flagged for de-scope rather than storified; threshold defined in the Definition of Ready.
All stories drafted for the epic (100% review), checked against the Definition of Ready and acceptance-criteria template.
Pass = every story has testable Given/When/Then AC, a linked parent requirement, and meets the Definition of Ready; fail if any story lacks AC or traceability.
Stories failing the DoR returned to Draft with a Jira comment listing gaps; owner = Business Analyst, 3-business-day fix SLA before re-review.
Acceptance: 100% of in-scope requirements covered by stories, each with testable AC, sized within the point ceiling, and accepted into the Ready backlog by the Product Owner.
Stories and AC live in Jira under the epic; the requirement-to-story traceability matrix is attached to the epic's Confluence page.
All elaborated requirements/stories in the Ready-for-Refinement queue for the upcoming sprint; scope = readiness assessment against the Definition of Ready before backlog prioritization.
Current refinement cycle; review completed before the sprint-planning session (typically 1-2 business days prior).
Each reviewed story must have populated: description, acceptance criteria, estimate, dependencies, and parent link; missing any field blocks the Ready transition.
Number of stories marked Ready equals number that passed the DoR checklist; 0 stories advanced with open DoR items.
Refinement outcomes (Ready/Not-Ready + notes) recorded on each Jira story with reviewer and timestamp; refinement session notes stored in Confluence with date.
Stories failing readiness logged as Not-Ready with a comment listing gaps; owner = Business Analyst, must be resolved before the next refinement or escalated to Product Owner.
Readiness assessed against the team's approved Definition of Ready (version-referenced in the team working agreement).
Stories above the size ceiling (e.g. > 8 points) are marked Not-Ready and returned for splitting; ceiling defined in the working agreement.
Stories below the minimum-value threshold flagged for de-prioritization; threshold defined in the backlog-management standard.
All stories in the Ready-for-Refinement queue for the sprint (100% review).
Pass = story meets every DoR item (clear AC, estimate, no unresolved dependency); fail if any DoR item is open.
Not-Ready stories returned to the BA with a gap list; 3-business-day fix SLA; unresolved blockers escalated to Product Owner at the next standup.
Acceptance: 100% of stories entering the sprint-candidate backlog pass the DoR, are sized within the ceiling, and have resolved dependencies.
Readiness verdicts recorded on each Jira story; refinement notes and the DoR checklist archived on the Confluence refinement page.

The integration/API under change (named service + interface contract); scope = all integration test cases covering the interface's request/response contract, error paths, auth, and non-functional (latency/throughput) requirements.
Certification for the current release candidate; integration test suite executed against the staging environment build promoted for this release.

Each Jira test execution must record: test case ID, linked acceptance criteria, environment/build version, result (pass/fail), and defect link on failure; all executions tied to the release test cycle.
Executed test count equals planned in-scope test count (0 not-run); pass rate = 100% of critical/high cases and >= agreed threshold for the full suite before certification.
Test execution report and contract-test results attached to the Jira release cycle with timestamp and build/commit SHA; certification record stored with the release artifact.
Every failed case linked to a Jira defect with severity and disposition (fix/waiver); waivers require sign-off and are logged on the release ticket with owner = Tech Lead.
The incoming demand/intake item vs. the full active product backlog and in-flight epics in Jira; scope = duplicate and overlap detection across open backlog items and recently closed work.
At intake, before triage; duplicate check completed within 2 business days of the demand being logged.

The demand record must have: title, description, requesting stakeholder, target value stream/component, and a completed duplicate-check field (searched keywords + linked candidates) before it can be triaged.
Duplicate search covers 100% of open backlog items in the target value stream plus closed items from the last 12 months; candidate matches logged as Jira 'relates to'/'duplicates' links.
Search query terms, results, and duplicate/overlap decision recorded on the demand Jira item with reviewer and timestamp.
Confirmed duplicates closed with 'Duplicate' resolution linked to the master item; partial overlaps logged as an exception for the Product Owner to merge or de-scope, 5-business-day decision SLA.

Engineering guilds/communities of practice across the Software Engineering & Delivery org (e.g. Backend, Frontend, DevOps, Testing CoPs); scope = running recurring knowledge-sharing sessions and capturing outputs.
Current quarter; each active CoP runs at least one session per sprint/bi-weekly cadence, with the quarter's session log complete by quarter end.
Each session record must include: date, CoP name, facilitator, topic, attendees, and a link to notes/recording in Confluence before it counts as delivered.
Number of logged sessions >= planned cadence per CoP for the quarter (e.g. >= 6 bi-weekly sessions); attendance reconciled against the CoP membership list.
Session notes/recordings stored in the CoP Confluence space with date and topic tag; retained for the current + prior year.
Missed/cancelled sessions logged as an exception on the CoP page with reason and owner = CoP facilitator; two consecutive misses escalated to the Platform Engineering Lead.
All CoP sessions scheduled for the quarter (100% review of the session log).
Pass = planned cadence met per CoP and every held session has notes/attendance captured; fail if cadence missed or sessions lack documented outputs.
Cadence shortfalls raised as an exception to the Platform Engineering Lead with a recovery plan; documentation gaps assigned to the facilitator with a 5-business-day fix SLA.
Acceptance: each active CoP met its documented cadence for the quarter and 100% of held sessions have notes and attendance recorded in Confluence.
Session logs, notes, and recordings in the CoP Confluence space; cadence/attendance summary tracked on the CoP dashboard page.
All stories in the current sprint with accepted acceptance criteria; scope = authoring functional test cases (positive, negative, boundary) traceable to each story's AC, then peer review.
Current sprint; test cases authored and reviewed before the corresponding story enters QA execution (no later than mid-sprint for early-pulled stories).
Each test case must have: unique ID, linked story/AC, preconditions, steps, expected result, and type (positive/negative/boundary) before it is submitted for review.
Every accepted AC maps to >= 1 test case (AC-to-test coverage = 100%; 0 uncovered AC); traceability matrix reconciles case count to AC count.
Authored cases and the AC-to-test traceability matrix stored in the test management tool / Jira test cycle with author, reviewer, and timestamp.
AC that cannot be covered (ambiguous/untestable) logged as an exception with owner = QA Analyst and routed back to the BA for clarification within 2 business days.
The release-candidate build artifact for the current release; scope = promoting the versioned artifact from the artifact repository into the test/staging environment for formal QA and UAT.
Current release cycle; promotion executed after CI green and before the QA/UAT window opens for the release.
Promotion record must capture: artifact name + immutable version/commit SHA, source pipeline run ID, target environment, and linked change ticket before the deploy runs.
Deployed artifact checksum/version in staging matches the artifact promoted from the repo (1:1); post-deploy smoke test passes 100% of critical health checks.
Pipeline deploy log, artifact version, and smoke-test results attached to the ServiceNow change ticket with timestamp; artifact retained immutably in the repo.

Failed promotion or smoke test triggers automatic rollback to the prior staging version; failure logged on the change ticket with owner = Release/Environment Manager and a fix-forward or retry decision within 1 business day.
Post-deploy smoke/health checks in staging compared to pre-deploy baseline; all critical endpoints healthy and version banner reflects the new build before sign-off.
Deploy linked to a ServiceNow change ticket (standard/normal change) referencing the release; no promotion to staging without a linked, approved change record.
The promoted artifact in staging (single build), validated via the automated smoke-test suite and environment health checks.
Pass = artifact version verified, smoke tests 100% green, environment healthy; fail = any smoke-test failure or version mismatch.
On fail, invoke instant rollback to prior version; reopen the promotion task and notify QA that UAT is blocked; escalate repeated failures to the Platform Engineering Lead.
Deployment follows the approved release/promotion runbook version referenced on the change ticket; IaC-defined environment config version pinned.
Artifact sourced from the CI/CD artifact repository (immutable, tagged by commit SHA); environment configuration sourced from the IaC repo for staging.

The solution design package for the initiative under review; scope = architecture diagrams (C4), interface/API contracts, data model, NFRs, security considerations, and ADRs assembled for the Architecture Review Board (ARB).
Prior to the scheduled ARB session for the initiative; package submitted no later than 5 business days before the review to allow reviewer pre-read.

Every triggered critical alert maps to exactly one incident ticket (no orphan alerts, no duplicate incidents); alert-to-incident reconciliation = 1:1 for the window.
Alert payload, incident timeline (detection, ack, escalation, resolution with UTC timestamps), and paging log retained in the ITSM platform, tagged with incident number; retained 24 months.
Alerts that are false positives closed with a 'false-positive' disposition and feed alert-tuning; missing runbook logged as 'SDLC-Exception', SRE lead owner, 10-business-day SLA.
Triage follows the approved incident-severity matrix v2 in the IR runbook; Sev1 = business-critical feed down, Sev2 = degraded with workaround.
Escalation to the next tier if not acknowledged within 15 minutes for Sev1 or 30 minutes for Sev2.
Sev1 declared when a regulatory/finance or customer-facing feed is fully blocked, or >=1000 policy/claims records miss the 06:00 SLA.
All critical alerts fired during the on-call window (the full incident set for the rotation).
PASS = Sev1 acknowledged <15 min and escalated per matrix, 100% of critical alerts have a triage disposition; FAIL = any Sev1 unacknowledged past 15 min or any critical alert with no incident ticket.
Unacknowledged Sev1 auto-escalates to the secondary on-call then the Engineering Manager; incidents lacking a runbook logged as 'SDLC-Exception' with 10-business-day remediation SLA.
Acceptance = every critical failure triaged with severity + owner within SLA, escalated per the matrix, and a resolution/handoff recorded.
Evidence = the incident timeline and paging log in the ITSM platform, cross-linked to the failing DAG's run in the orchestration/observability tool.

All production data pipelines orchestrated in the ITSM/scheduler with a business SLA tier (P1 finance/regulatory feeds, P2 analytics, P3 internal). Scope = the failed or late DAG run plus every downstream dependent job in the same lineage.
The current scheduling window for the affected run (e.g. nightly 02:00-06:00 ET batch load) up to the point the pipeline is confirmed recovered and caught up to the current watermark.

Post-recovery row counts and control totals for the re-run match the source watermark within 0 variance for financial feeds and <=0.1% for analytics feeds; reconciliation query result attached to the incident.
Scheduler run log, error stack trace, and reconciliation output exported to the incident record with UTC timestamp and pipeline commit SHA; retained per the incident's 3-year audit retention.

Every SLA breach logged as an ITSM incident with disposition (recovered / re-run / data-quarantine / permanent-fail-escalated) and, if unresolved within the SLA tier, escalated to on-call SRE and the data product owner.
Runbook and recovery procedure for the pipeline are the latest approved version in Confluence, referenced by id in the incident; recovery steps executed match the approved runbook revision.
Alert thresholds: warn at 50% of SLA window elapsed with job still running, page on-call at 80%; late-data threshold = watermark lag > 30 min for P1, > 2 h for P2.
Any pipeline feeding a regulatory or GL filing is material; a missed P1 SLA or >0 reconciliation variance on a material feed triggers mandatory data product owner sign-off before close.
Sample of the last 20 SLA-breach incidents over the trailing quarter, weighted to include all P1 breaches.
Pass = pipeline recovered within its SLA tier (P1 <=2 h, P2 <=8 h, P3 next business day) and reconciliation clean; fail = SLA missed or reconciliation variance outside tolerance.

On persistent failure, quarantine partial output, open a P1 SDLC-Exception ticket owned by the Engineering Manager with a 10-business-day RCA SLA, and notify downstream data consumers via the ITSM broadcast.
Recovery executed against the runbook version tagged in the pipeline repo (git tag matching the deployed release), recorded in the incident.
Scheduler config and connection parameters sourced from the version-controlled IaC repo and the secrets vault; no manual parameter overrides permitted during recovery.

High-traffic and latency-sensitive components identified in the release scope (public APIs, quote/bind endpoints, batch ingestion). Scope = the specific service build/tag under test plus its direct downstream dependencies.
The performance test campaign for the current release candidate, run in the pre-production performance environment before the go/no-go gate.
Every scenario records p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (req/s), error rate, and resource utilisation; all fields populated in the test report before results are accepted.
Requests issued vs. responses recorded reconcile within 0.1%; unaccounted requests investigated and explained before the run is deemed valid.
Test plan, load profile, raw result files, and dashboards exported to the CI artifact store tagged with the build SHA and UTC run timestamp; retained for the release's audit window.
Any scenario breaching a target logged as a defect in Jira with severity, owner, and disposition (fix / accept-with-waiver / block-release).
Current-release p95 latency and throughput compared against the prior release baseline; no more than 5% latency regression permitted, and any regression waived requires Tech Lead sign-off.
Performance run linked to the release change ticket (Jira release id / change record) and to the CI pipeline run that produced the tested build.
The full set of performance scenarios for the release: steady-state load, peak (2x expected), soak (2 h), and spike; each executed against the tagged build.
Pass = p95 <= 500 ms, p99 <= 1 s, error rate < 0.1% at target throughput, and no > 5% regression vs. baseline; fail = any target breached.

On failure, block the release gate and open a Jira defect (type Performance) owned by the Tech Lead; a waiver requires an SDLC-Exception ticket approved by the Engineering Manager with a remediation plan and 10-business-day SLA.
Effective for the current release candidate; results expire and must be re-run if the build SHA changes before deployment.
The streaming pipeline under test (e.g. Kafka topic + stream processor) and its consumers. Scope = the deployed stream job version validated against peak-condition throughput and latency targets.
The load-test campaign for the current stream release candidate, executed in the staging streaming cluster before promotion.
Each run records sustained events/sec, end-to-end latency (p95/p99), consumer lag, and dropped-message count; all fields populated before results accepted.
Messages produced vs. consumed reconcile with 0 message loss at target rate; any gap between produced and committed offsets investigated before pass.
Load profile, throughput/latency dashboards, and consumer-lag charts exported to the CI artifact store with build SHA and UTC timestamp; retained for the release audit window.
Any breach of latency or lag target logged as a Jira defect with severity, owner, and disposition (tune / scale / block-release).
Current-version throughput and p99 latency compared to prior baseline; no > 5% latency or lag regression permitted without Tech Lead sign-off.
Peak-condition scenarios: sustained target rate, 2x burst, and a partition-rebalance during load, each against the tagged stream job.
Pass = sustains target events/sec with p99 latency <= 2 s, consumer lag draining to 0 within 60 s of burst end, and 0 message loss; fail = any target breached.
On failure, block promotion and open a Jira defect owned by the Tech Lead; waiver via SDLC-Exception ticket approved by Engineering Manager with a 10-business-day remediation SLA.
Effective for the current stream job version; re-run required if the deployed artifact changes before promotion.
Demand items in the intake backlog flagged high-priority or high-risk (regulatory, security, or executive-sponsored). Scope = the specific demand record being escalated to technology leadership.

Versioning follows the current approved docs-as-code branching/tagging standard referenced in the repo README.
Document content sourced from the reviewed, signed-off versions in Confluence/GRC; the committed version matches the approved review artifact.

All third-party/partner integration endpoints registered in the API gateway (Azure API Management) for ABC Insurance production and non-prod, plus all outbound connections defined in the source repo's integration config; scope = every partner endpoint with an active connection agreement (reinsurers, bureaus, payment processors, Guidewire cloud interfaces).

Count of items marked 'Ready' reconciles with items passing all DoR checklist fields; no item is 'Ready' with an unmet DoR field.

All public and internal API/interface reference docs for services shipping in this release; scope = every REST/event endpoint with a versioned OpenAPI/AsyncAPI spec in the source repo, plus SDK/interface guides in Confluence.

Published doc bundle tagged with the release version and git SHA, retained in Confluence with page history; superseded versions archived, not deleted.

Classification recorded on the ITSM record with the classifying agent and timestamp; category taxonomy version noted; audit trail retained per record-retention policy.
Misclassified or ambiguous requests are re-triaged with the correction and rationale logged in the ITSM work notes.
Requests touching regulated data or access changes cite the applicable policy/rule (e.g., internal access-control policy; NYDFS 500 §500.7 for access requests) in the ITSM record.
ITSM records retained per the enterprise records-retention schedule (security/audit-relevant tickets ≥3 years) with immutable work-note history.
Classification completed within the intake SLA (e.g., 4 business hours for standard, 1 hour for high-priority) so downstream fulfillment SLAs remain achievable.
All service requests received in the period (typically 20-100 tickets).
Pass = ≥98% of requests fully classified (type, priority, team) within the classification SLA; fail = any request routed with a missing attribute or classified late.
A request that cannot be classified (unknown type) is escalated to the service desk lead via an ITSM 'TRIAGE-Exception' and resolved within 1 business day.
A request is 'classified' when type, priority, and fulfilling team are set, any required policy citation is attached, and it is routed to the correct queue.
Classification attributes and history on the ITSM record; period classification-quality summary on the service-desk dashboard.

All elaborated user stories/requirements for the current epic in the Jira project (project key of the initiative), status 'Ready for Review', linked to the parent epic; excludes stories in 'Draft' or 'Backlog'.
The active elaboration window = current PI/increment start date through the sprint in which the story is committed (e.g., 2026-Q3 PI, Sprints 3-5).

Each requirement has non-empty acceptance criteria (Gherkin Given/When/Then), a testable definition of done, and a linked business owner; validate via Jira required-field automation blocking transition to 'Validated' if any field is empty.
Count of stories reviewed in the validation session equals count of stories dispositioned (Accepted/Changed/Rejected) in the Jira review log; 0 stories left un-dispositioned at session close.

Signed validation minutes and per-story feedback exported to Confluence under the epic space, filename '<EPIC>-requirements-validation-vN', page version and timestamp recorded; attachments retained 3 years.
Every disputed requirement logged as a Jira sub-task type 'Requirement-Clarification' with disposition (accepted/rework/deferred), assignee, and due date within 5 business days.
Requirements elaboration follows BABOK v3 elicitation method version documented on the Confluence 'BA Playbook' page v2.1; method version recorded on each story.
Any change to acceptance criteria affecting >20% of a story's scope triggers mandatory re-validation with the business owner.
Requirements affecting regulated flows (rating, claims payout, PII handling) are flagged 'material' and require compliance reviewer sign-off before build.
Validation decision (approved/rework) recorded on the epic's Jira 'Validation' field with reviewer, date, and link to the Confluence minutes.
Distribution list = product owner, assigned engineers (backend + UI), business owner, and scrum master; notified via Jira @mention and Teams channel #<initiative>-delivery.
100% of stories marked 'Ready for Review' in the current PI (typically 15-40 stories/sprint).
PASS = every story has approved acceptance criteria, testable DoD, business-owner sign-off; FAIL = any missing → story returned to elaboration. Target ≥95% first-pass approval.
Failed stories moved to 'Needs Rework' with a Jira 'Requirement-Clarification' sub-task; 5-business-day remediation SLA; escalate to Product Owner if breached.
Current PI/sprint effective dates as recorded on the Jira board (sprint start/end).
All inbound technology demand/change requests submitted via the ServiceNow Demand catalog item 'IT Demand Intake' for the current fiscal quarter; excludes standard operational incidents.
Rolling intake window = current fiscal quarter to date (e.g., FY26 Q3).

Each demand record has: requester, sponsoring business unit, problem statement, desired outcome, affected application (CMDB CI reference), and priority; ServiceNow mandatory-field validation blocks submission if any are blank.
Number of intake emails/forms received in the shared queue equals number of ServiceNow demand records created; reconcile daily, 0 unlogged requests older than 1 business day.
Demand record auto-timestamped on creation with unique DMND number and requester; ServiceNow retains full audit history (created/updated by/on) for 3 years.
Incomplete or out-of-scope requests set to state 'Clarification Needed' with a work note stating the gap and returned to requester; 3-business-day SLA to re-submit.
100% of demand records created in the quarter (sample all if <200, else statistically valid sample of 50).
PASS = record has requester, business unit, outcome, CMDB CI, and priority populated and a unique DMND id; FAIL = any missing. Target ≥98% complete on first logging.
Failed records flagged 'Clarification Needed'; requester notified via ServiceNow email; unresolved >5 business days escalated to Demand Manager/PMO.
Acceptance criterion for this task = a uniquely numbered ServiceNow demand record exists with all mandatory fields populated and requester acknowledgement captured.
Evidence = the ServiceNow demand record URL and its audit log; exported quarterly to the PPM tool (Clarity/Planview) demand register.
The specific project/sprint being kicked off = the committed sprint backlog in the Jira board for the current sprint (sprint id and goal named in the sprint), scoped to the approved epic(s).
Sprint duration = 2 weeks (current sprint start/end dates from the Jira board).
Sprint has: named goal, committed stories with estimates, assigned owners, and a linked repository/CI pipeline; Jira sprint start blocked until goal field and ≥1 committed story exist.
Sum of committed story points ≤ team's rolling 3-sprint average velocity ±15%; capacity vs. commitment reconciled at planning.
Sprint planning minutes and commitment recorded in Confluence '<team>-sprint-<n>' page and the Jira sprint report, timestamped at sprint start.
Stories not meeting Definition of Ready are excluded from the sprint and returned to backlog with a 'Not Ready' label and reason note.
All stories proposed for the sprint (typically 8-15 stories).
PASS = sprint goal set, all committed stories meet Definition of Ready, capacity ≥ commitment; FAIL = any unmet. Target: sprint starts with 0 not-ready stories committed.
If capacity < commitment or DoR not met, scope is reduced at planning; unresolved blockers escalated to Scrum Master and Product Owner same day.
Sprint effective dates = current sprint start and end as recorded in Jira.
All open defects with type 'Defect' and phase label 'Integration Test' logged against the current release in Jira, severity Critical/High/Medium; scoped to the release fix version.
Current integration-test cycle for the release (fix version window, e.g., release 26.3 hardening sprint).
Each defect has: reproduction steps, environment, root-cause note, linked PR/commit, and re-test evidence; Jira workflow blocks 'Closed' until 'Root Cause' and 'Fix Commit' fields are populated.
Count of defects marked 'Fixed' equals count with a linked merged PR and a passing re-test result; 0 defects closed without a linked verification run.
Fix PR, CI run id, and re-test result attached to each defect; integration-test pipeline logs retained in Azure DevOps/GitHub Actions run history with timestamp and commit SHA.
Defects that cannot be fixed in-cycle are dispositioned as 'Deferred' with a risk note and Release Manager approval; recorded as a known-issue in the release notes.
Defect-resolution workflow follows the team's defect-management SOP v1.3 in Confluence; workflow version referenced on the release.
Any fix touching >200 changed lines or a shared integration contract triggers a full integration regression run, not just the targeted test.
Critical/High severity = release-blocking (must be fixed or formally waived); Medium = fix or defer with sign-off; Low = backlog.
All defects in the integration-test cycle for the release (all Critical/High plus a sample of Medium).
PASS = defect fix merged, targeted + regression integration tests green in CI, contract tests pass; FAIL = any red test. Exit criteria: 0 open Critical/High at release gate.

Failed re-test reopens the defect and blocks the release build; unresolved Critical/High escalate to Release Manager; deferrals require a 'SDLC-Exception' Jira ticket approved by the Engineering Manager.
Integration-test cycle dates for the current release fix version.
The candidate features/epics under consideration for the upcoming PI, as listed in the Jira backlog with label 'prioritization-candidate'; scoped to the current planning horizon.
Planning horizon = next PI/quarter (e.g., FY26 Q4).

The delivery-approach proposal states, per candidate: recommended approach (build/buy/phased/MVP), rough effort, key dependencies, risks, and sequencing rationale; template fields all populated in the Confluence proposal page.
Every prioritization candidate on the backlog has a corresponding delivery-approach recommendation; count of candidates equals count of recommendations, 0 unaddressed.
Proposal saved to Confluence '<PI>-delivery-approach-vN' with version and timestamp, and attached to the PI-planning Jira epic.
Candidates lacking enough information to recommend an approach are flagged 'Needs Discovery' with a spike ticket and owner; 5-business-day SLA to scope.
All prioritization candidates for the upcoming PI (typically 5-12 epics).

PASS = each candidate has a recommended approach with effort, dependencies, and risks documented; FAIL = any candidate without a rationale. Target 100% of candidates covered before the prioritization meeting.
Under-scoped candidates deferred to a discovery spike; if a decision is needed without data, escalate to the Product Owner/architecture review for a provisional recommendation.
Acceptance criterion = a delivery-approach recommendation exists for every candidate, reviewed by a Tech Lead, ready to present at the prioritization discussion.
Evidence = the Confluence proposal page and its link on the PI-planning Jira epic.

The current-state processes and pain points for the in-scope value stream/application, as captured in workshops with named SMEs from the affected business units; scope defined on the workshop charter.
Discovery phase window for the initiative (e.g., 3-week discovery, dates on the initiative plan).
Each workshop output has: attendee list, current-state process map, documented pain points with owner, and identified data sources; findings template fully populated in Confluence.
Every scheduled workshop session has a corresponding findings page; count of held sessions equals count of documented outputs, 0 sessions undocumented.
Workshop notes, process maps, and recordings saved to Confluence '<initiative>-current-state-discovery' with page version and date; retained per project record policy.
Open questions/unvalidated findings logged as Jira 'Discovery-Followup' items with owner and due date; 5-business-day SLA to resolve or confirm.
Discovery follows the BA Playbook v2.1 workshop facilitation method; method version cited on the charter.
Findings that materially change scope or reveal a new regulated data flow trigger a scope re-baseline and stakeholder review.
Pain points affecting customer data, financial accuracy, or regulatory reporting are tagged 'high-impact' and prioritized for the future-state design.
All workshop sessions held in the discovery phase and their findings pages.
PASS = every session documented with process map, pain points, and SME sign-off; FAIL = any missing artifact. Target 100% of sessions documented within 2 business days of the session.
Undocumented or disputed findings raised as 'Discovery-Followup' Jira items; unresolved >5 business days escalated to the Product Owner.
Source-system fields referenced in current-state maps are defined against the data catalog (business + technical metadata) for the affected systems.
Where volume claims are made (e.g., transactions/day), they are validated against a source-system count from the enterprise data warehouse, not estimated.

All significant architecture/design decisions for the initiative requiring an ADR (per the ADR trigger criteria: cross-team impact, new technology, data-model change, security-relevant choice); stored in the repo /docs/adr folder.
Current design/build phase of the initiative (PI window).
Each ADR uses the standard template (Context, Decision, Status, Consequences, Alternatives) with all sections non-empty; a CI docs-lint check fails the PR if a required section is blank.
Every decision meeting the ADR trigger has a corresponding numbered ADR; reconcile decision log vs. /docs/adr, 0 significant decisions without an ADR.
ADRs stored as versioned Markdown in the Git repo with sequential ids (ADR-0001…), commit history providing timestamp/author; retained for the life of the system.
Superseded decisions marked Status='Superseded by ADR-NNNN' rather than deleted; open questions tracked as 'Proposed' status ADRs with owner.
ADR format follows the Michael Nygard ADR template adopted in the engineering handbook v3.0; template version referenced in /docs/adr/README.md.
Decisions with cross-domain or security impact require Architecture Review Board (ARB) review before the ADR is accepted.
Decisions affecting more than one bounded context/team, or introducing a new vendor/technology, are 'material' and require Enterprise Architect sign-off.
All ADRs produced for the initiative in the current phase.

PASS = ADR has all template sections, a decision status, and links to affected components; FAIL = any missing section or unlinked significant decision. Target: 100% of significant decisions have an accepted ADR before build.
Incomplete ADRs blocked at PR review by the docs-lint gate; material decisions without ARB sign-off cannot move to Status='Accepted'; escalate unresolved to the Enterprise Architect.
Where an ADR references data entities/interfaces, field and interface definitions cite the data catalog / OpenAPI spec of record.
Not applicable to control totals; instead each ADR is cross-checked against the current system C4 diagram to confirm the described components exist.
The feature/story code changes for the assigned Jira story, delivered as one or more pull requests against the service repository; scope bounded by the story's acceptance criteria.
Current sprint in which the story is committed (sprint dates from the Jira board).
Code satisfies acceptance criteria, passes linters/formatter (Prettier/Black), has unit tests for changed lines, and includes a linked Jira id; PR template checklist enforced before merge.
Code coverage on changed lines ≥ 80% (SonarQube diff coverage) and all CI checks green; PR cannot merge if the quality gate fails.
Merged commit SHA, PR number, CI run id, and SonarQube analysis link recorded on the Jira story; CI run history retained in GitHub Enterprise/Azure DevOps.

Deviations from coding standards logged as SonarQube issues; unavoidable exceptions require a code comment plus a 'SDLC-Exception' Jira ticket approved by the Engineering Manager (10-business-day remediation SLA).
All changed/added code in the story's pull request(s).
PASS = all acceptance criteria met, CI green (build+unit+integration), SonarQube quality gate passed (0 new critical/high issues, diff coverage ≥80%), ≥1 approving review; FAIL = any gate red.

Failing gate blocks merge; SonarQube new-code issues must be fixed or waived via 'SDLC-Exception' (Engineering Manager approval, 10-business-day SLA); flaky-test failures triaged and re-run, persistent failures escalated to Tech Lead.
Implementation follows the coding standards handbook v3.0 and the design/ADR pinned to the story.
Configuration values externalized (no hardcoded secrets/endpoints); sourced from environment config / secrets manager, not committed to the repo.
The delivery team roster for the initiative and the required environments (dev, test/QA, staging) with their access, tooling, and pipeline readiness; scope defined on the team charter.
Sprint 0 / mobilization window before the first delivery sprint.

Every required role is filled with a named person and access granted; each environment (dev/test/staging) is provisioned, reachable, and has a green pipeline; readiness checklist fields all ticked in Confluence.
Number of required roles equals number of confirmed assignments; number of required environments equals number verified healthy; 0 gaps at kickoff.
Team roster (with IAM access grants) and environment readiness results saved to Confluence '<initiative>-mobilization-readiness' with timestamp; CMDB updated with environment CIs.
Unfilled roles or unavailable environments logged as Jira 'Mobilization-Blocker' items with owner and target date; blockers >5 business days escalated to the Resource Manager/PMO.
All required roles and all required environments for the initiative.
PASS = all roles filled with access granted AND all environments provisioned with green smoke tests; FAIL = any role or environment gap. Target: 100% readiness before Sprint 1 start.
Any gap logged as a 'Mobilization-Blocker'; Sprint 1 start deferred or scope reduced if critical roles/environments are not ready; escalate to PMO/Resource Manager.
Mobilization window dates immediately preceding Sprint 1.

All documentation pages/artifacts identified as superseded or obsolete for the system (Confluence spaces + repo /docs) that have a newer replacement; scope = the documentation set for the initiative/system under review.
Documentation review cycle for the release (e.g., end-of-release hardening/close-out).

Each archived doc is tagged 'Archived', carries a replacement reference (link to the current doc) and a sunset date, and is moved to the Confluence 'Archive' space; a page-property report enforces these three fields.
Count of docs identified as superseded equals count archived with replacement reference + sunset date; 0 superseded docs left in active spaces without a redirect.

Archive action logged with page version, archiver, date, and replacement link; Confluence page history and the repo commit (for /docs moves) provide the timestamped trail; retained per records policy.
Docs still linked from active content are redirected before archiving; unresolved references logged as Jira 'Doc-Cleanup' items with owner and 10-business-day SLA.
All documents flagged as superseded in the review cycle.

PASS = doc archived, tagged 'Archived', has a working replacement link and a sunset date, and no active page links to it un-redirected; FAIL = any missing. Target 100% of superseded docs correctly archived.
Docs with unresolved inbound links are held (not archived) and a 'Doc-Cleanup' Jira item is created; escalate to Tech Lead if links remain broken >10 business days.
Where archived docs describe data entities/interfaces, the replacement reference points to the current source of truth (data catalog / OpenAPI spec).
Not applicable to control totals; instead verify the link graph: number of inbound links to each archived doc = 0 (all redirected) at close.
All engineering squads in the value stream that closed a sprint in the period; one retrospective per squad per sprint, tracked as Jira issue type 'Retrospective' under the team's board.
The two-week sprint just closed (sprint end date minus 13 calendar days through sprint end date); retro held within 3 business days of sprint close.

Each retro record must have: sprint id, attendee list, at least 3 'what went well' items, at least 3 'what to improve' items, and >=1 action item with an owner and due date; Confluence retro page linked from the Jira retro issue.
Count of retros held = count of squads with a closed sprint in the period; reconcile the Jira retro-issue count against the sprint-report count with 0 variance.
Confluence retro page version timestamp plus the Jira retro issue transition-to-Done timestamp retained for 24 months in the team space.
Any squad that skipped a retro is logged as a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' with reason and a make-up date within 5 business days; owner = Scrum Master.
All sprint retrospectives held in the reporting quarter across the value stream's squads (typically 20-30 retro records).
Pass = 100% of closed sprints have a linked retro record with >=1 owned action item; fail if <100%. Action-item carryover into the next sprint must be >=70% closed.
Missing or incomplete retro raises a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' assigned to the Scrum Master with a 5-business-day remediation SLA.
Jira fields: Sprint (sprint id), Issue Type = Retrospective, Assignee (facilitator), Linked Confluence page URL; Confluence retro template columns Went Well / Improve / Action / Owner / Due.
Sprint-report squad count for the period sourced from Jira; used as the control total against retro-issue count.

Knowledge outputs produced from every sprint retrospective in the period: lessons learned, action items, and reusable engineering guidance, published to the team Confluence space and cross-linked from the Jira retro issue.
The sprint just closed; outputs recorded within 3 business days of the retro.
Each output record must have: source sprint id, category (lesson/action/pattern), owner, and a Confluence page URL; action items must have a due date and Jira link.
Number of published knowledge pages = number of retros held in the period; reconcile Confluence page count to Jira retro-issue count with 0 variance.
Confluence page version + last-modified timestamp retained 24 months; export saved to the team space page tree under 'Retrospective Outputs'.
Any retro with no captured output logged as Jira 'SDLC-Exception', owner = Scrum Master, 5-business-day remediation SLA.
All retrospective knowledge pages published in the reporting quarter across the value stream's squads.
Pass = 100% of retros have a linked, categorized Confluence output page with owned action items; fail if <100%.
Missing output page raises a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' assigned to the Scrum Master with a 5-business-day remediation SLA.
Confluence 'Retrospective Outputs' template fields: Source Sprint, Category, Description, Owner, Linked Jira, Due Date; page labelled 'retro-output'.
Jira retro-issue count for the period used as the control total against the count of 'retro-output'-labelled Confluence pages.

All implementation-governance decisions and design-assurance gate outcomes for changes deployed in the reporting period across the value stream; each gate outcome recorded in the GRC platform as a governance record linked to its change ticket.
The reporting quarter (calendar quarter just ended); leadership report delivered within 10 business days of quarter close.
Each governance record must have: change ticket id, gate name, outcome (pass/conditional/fail), reviewer, date, and remediation status; open exceptions must carry a due date and owner.
Number of governance records in the report = number of deployed changes requiring a gate in the period; reconcile GRC record count to the change-ticket count with 0 variance.
Report PDF plus underlying GRC export retained 7 years in the compliance evidence repository, versioned with quarter tag (e.g. 'GovReport-2026Q2-v1').
Any gate failure or unremediated finding logged as a GRC issue with disposition (accepted/remediating/waived); owner = Enterprise Architect; waivers require ARB approval.
Prior-quarter governance metrics compared against current quarter (gate pass rate, mean remediation days); variance and trend explained in the report narrative.
Each governance record links to its ServiceNow/Jira change ticket id; unlinked records are a reconciliation defect and must be resolved before the report is finalized.
All governance gate outcomes recorded in the GRC platform for the reporting quarter.
Pass = report reconciles 100% to GRC records and every finding has a disposition; fail if any record lacks an outcome, reviewer, or disposition.
Discrepancy between report and GRC data raises a GRC issue assigned to the Enterprise Architect with a 5-business-day remediation SLA before sign-off.
Delegation matrix in the GRC platform maps each gate to its approving authority (ARB chair, Enterprise Architect, CISO for security gates) with named backups; reviewed quarterly.
All functional and non-functional requirements for the feature/epic being built, elicited from the Product Owner and named SMEs; captured as Jira stories under the epic with acceptance criteria.
The elaboration window for the current program increment / sprint intake; requirements agreed before the story enters 'Ready for Dev'.
All items archived in the current run; 100% inspected for required closure metadata.
Every story must have: a user-story statement, testable acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then), Product Owner sign-off, and links to any SME source docs in Confluence.
Count of agreed stories = count of scoped requirements from the intake list; reconcile Jira story count to the requirements register with 0 unmapped items.
Confluence requirements page version timestamp + Jira story history retained for the project lifetime + 24 months in the team space.

Ambiguous or contested requirements logged as Jira 'Clarification' sub-tasks with owner and due date; unresolved items block 'Ready for Dev' and are raised as 'SDLC-Exception' if aging >5 business days.
All stories in the epic intended for the upcoming sprint(s).
Pass = 100% of stories entering the sprint have PO-approved, testable acceptance criteria; fail if any story lacks acceptance criteria or PO sign-off.
Requirement gaps found during dev raise a Jira 'Clarification' assigned to the Business Analyst; if unresolved in 5 business days, escalate as 'SDLC-Exception' to the Product Owner.
Jira story fields: Summary, Description (user story), Acceptance Criteria (custom field), Epic Link, Linked Confluence requirement page; INVEST criteria applied at refinement.
Requirements register (Confluence table) row count for the epic used as the control total against Jira story count.
The set of stories proposed for the upcoming sprint plus the squad's capacity for that sprint; validated in Jira against team velocity and member availability.
The upcoming two-week sprint; feasibility confirmed during sprint planning before commitment is locked.
Each candidate story must have story points estimated, no unresolved blockers, and a defined acceptance criterion; team capacity must account for PTO, ceremonies, and support load.
Committed story points must be <= rolling 3-sprint average velocity; reconcile committed points against capacity-adjusted velocity with the delta shown in the sprint planning notes.
Sprint planning Confluence note (capacity, velocity, commitment) versioned and timestamped; retained 24 months in the team space and linked from the sprint in Jira.
Over-commitment (committed points > 110% of capacity-adjusted velocity) logged as a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' with justification; owner = Scrum Master; requires Product Owner acknowledgement.
All stories proposed for the upcoming sprint (the planning candidate set).
Pass = committed points within 90-110% of capacity-adjusted velocity and 100% of committed stories estimated and blocker-free; fail otherwise.
Infeasible commitment triggers descope negotiation with the Product Owner; residual over-commitment logged as 'SDLC-Exception' owned by the Scrum Master with a same-sprint resolution SLA.
The upcoming sprint's start and end dates as defined in Jira; capacity computed for exactly those working days.

Developer experience metrics for the reporting quarter across all engineering squads: DORA metrics (deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, MTTR), PR cycle time, build success rate, and developer-survey scores; sourced into the enterprise data warehouse.
The reporting quarter (calendar quarter just ended); report delivered to leadership within 10 business days of quarter close.
Every metric must have: a definition, source system, calculation window, unit, and target/benchmark; DORA metrics computed per the standard four-key definitions with no nulls in the reporting rows.
Metric row counts in the BI report reconcile to source-system extracts (pipeline, Jira, survey tool) with variance <= 1%; totals footed against the warehouse fact tables.
Report snapshot (BI export + query definitions) versioned with quarter tag and retained 24 months in the reporting repository; data lineage captured in the data catalog.
Any metric with a data-quality gap or missing source is footnoted and logged as a Jira 'SDLC-Exception'; owner = Data Engineer; 10-business-day remediation SLA.
All developer-experience metric records for the reporting quarter across squads.
Pass = report reconciles to source extracts within 1% and every metric has a definition and target; fail if any headline metric is unreconciled or undefined.
Reconciliation break raises a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' assigned to the Data Engineer with a 5-business-day remediation SLA before the report is released.
Delegation matrix in the reporting repository names the Tech Lead as report approver and the Data Engineer as data-owner backup; reviewed quarterly.
The release candidate's completed scope: all stories in the release meeting the Definition of Done, requiring Product Owner acceptance sign-off before the RC tag is cut.
The release window for the current increment; sign-off recorded before the release branch/tag is cut.
Every RC story must show acceptance criteria met, UAT/demo evidence linked, and no open blocker defects; sign-off record must name the approver, date, and RC version.
Count of accepted stories = count of stories in the release scope; reconcile Jira 'Accepted' stories to the release scope list with 0 unaccepted in-scope items.
Sign-off recorded as a Jira transition + Confluence release-acceptance page, versioned with the RC tag, retained 24 months in the release space.
Any story accepted with a known limitation logged as a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' with disposition and a follow-up ticket; owner = Product Owner.
Acceptance decision documented on the Confluence release-acceptance page: approver, date, RC version, scope accepted, and any conditions; linked from the Jira release.
Sign-off notification sent to Release Manager, Tech Lead, and QA Lead via the release Jira issue watchers and the #release channel; recipients recorded on the acceptance page.
All stories in the release-candidate scope.
Pass = Product Owner acceptance recorded for 100% of in-scope stories with no open blocker defects; fail if any in-scope story is unaccepted or a blocker is open.
Missing sign-off blocks the RC cut; a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' is raised to the Product Owner with a same-day remediation SLA before release proceeds.
Delegation matrix in the release space names the Product Owner as acceptance authority and a designated proxy PO as backup; RC cut authority held by the Release Manager, reviewed each release.

Real-time ingestion jobs for the in-scope streaming sources (e.g. policy/claims/billing event topics on Kafka); each job reads a named source topic and lands raw records to the Bronze/landing layer of the lakehouse.
The build sprint for the streaming pipeline; job considered done when it runs continuously against source topics in the non-prod environment for >=24 hours without unhandled failures.

Ingestion job config must specify: source topic/connection, schema (registered in the schema registry), checkpoint/offset store, dead-letter topic, and idempotency key; all required config keys present and validated in CI.
Records consumed from the source topic reconcile to records landed in Bronze within the watermark window; consumer-lag and landed-count delta <= 0.1% over a 24-hour soak.
Job manifest, schema version, and soak-test run logs committed to the repo and retained with the build artifact; pipeline run id and timestamp recorded in the CI/CD system.

Malformed or unprocessable records routed to a dead-letter topic and logged; any sustained lag or DLQ growth raises a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' owned by the Data Engineer with a 5-business-day remediation SLA.

Real-time transformation jobs applied to ingested streams: cleansing, enrichment, and business-rule transforms that read Bronze/landing records and produce Silver/curated output topics or tables in the lakehouse.
The build sprint for the streaming transforms; job done when it produces validated output continuously against ingested streams for >=24 hours in non-prod.

Transform config must specify: input Bronze source, output schema, windowing/watermark strategy, data-quality rules, and error/DLQ handling; all required transform parameters present and validated in CI.
Input record count reconciles to output + filtered + DLQ counts (conservation of records) within 0.1% over a 24-hour soak; row-level checksums sampled for enrichment accuracy.
Transform code, unit/integration test results, and soak-test lineage committed to the repo and retained with the artifact; run id and timestamp in the CI/CD system.
Records failing DQ rules routed to a quarantine/DLQ table with reason codes; recurring failures raise a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' owned by the Data Engineer with a 5-business-day remediation SLA.
All blocking dependencies identified on backlog items proposed for the upcoming sprint; each blocker tracked as a Jira issue link ('is blocked by') on its story.
The refinement-to-planning window for the upcoming sprint; blockers cleared before items enter the sprint commitment.
Each blocker must have: a linked blocking issue, an owner, a target resolution date, and a status; a story is 'Ready' only when all its blocking links are resolved or explicitly waived.
Count of open blockers on sprint-candidate stories must reach 0 (or documented waiver) before commitment; reconcile the Jira blocker-link report to the candidate story list.
Blocker resolution history retained in Jira issue links + comments; a dependency-status snapshot saved to the sprint planning Confluence note, versioned and timestamped.
Unresolved blockers at planning logged as a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' with owner and escalation; the blocked story is descoped or the blocker escalated to the Scrum Master with a same-sprint SLA.
All stories proposed for the upcoming sprint that carry one or more 'is blocked by' links.
Pass = 0 open blockers (or all waived with justification) on committed stories; fail if any committed story has an unresolved blocking link.
