A blocker that cannot be cleared before planning triggers descope or escalation as a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' owned by the Scrum Master with a same-sprint remediation SLA.
Acceptance: every sprint-candidate story has zero unresolved blocking dependencies at commitment, evidenced by the Jira blocker-link report showing all links resolved or waived.
Evidence: Jira blocker-link report filter 'Sprint Candidates - Open Blockers' plus the dependency snapshot on the sprint planning Confluence note.
All defects in Jira with status 'Ready for Re-test' resolved against build artifact of the current release candidate (repo main branch, tagged rc-x.y.z); one re-test execution per defect.
Current sprint window and the active release train cycle (e.g. Sprint 2026.07, Release 26.3), covering all defects moved to 'Fixed' since the last re-test cycle.

Every re-test record carries: defect key, build/tag re-tested against, test case ID, actual result, pass/fail verdict, tester, and timestamp; no record may be saved without a linked test-case execution.
Count of defects marked 'Fixed' at cycle start reconciles exactly to count of re-test executions recorded (delta = 0); any un-re-tested 'Fixed' defect blocks the release gate.

Re-test evidence (execution log, screenshots, console/API output) attached to the Jira defect and to the Xray/Zephyr test execution, stamped with build tag and UTC timestamp; retained per release for 12 months.

Defects that fail re-test are re-opened, assigned back to the fixing developer with 'reopened' label, and logged in the release exception register; blocked/untestable items get a 'test-blocked' Jira ticket with owner and target date.

For each re-tested defect the failing pre-fix behavior no longer reproduces and the documented expected result is observed on the fixed build; regression suite for the affected module re-run with 0 new failures.
Each re-test links to the originating defect (Jira DEF-#) and to the change/PR that delivered the fix; verify the fix commit SHA in the re-tested build matches the merged PR.
All defects flagged 'Fixed / Ready for Re-test' in the current release train; 100% must be re-tested, not sampled.

PASS = documented expected result observed and no regression in the module suite; FAIL = original defect reproduces or any new regression appears. Release gate requires 100% of re-tested defects PASS or explicitly deferred with sign-off.
Failed re-test -> re-open defect to developer with reopened label; untestable -> raise 'test-blocked' Jira ticket, owner = QA Lead, resolve within 2 business days or escalate to Release Manager.
Re-test results are valid only for the exact build tag re-tested (rc-x.y.z); a new build supersedes prior re-test evidence and requires re-execution before release.
The single approved pull request targeting the mainline (main/develop) in the service repository, containing only reviewed and CI-green changes for the feature/fix under delivery.
Current sprint / release train iteration; merge performed within the iteration once all merge-gate conditions are satisfied.

PR has: >=2 approvals, all conversations resolved, linked Jira work item, green required checks (build, unit, SAST, coverage), and a Conventional Commit title; merge blocked until all are true via branch protection.
Post-merge mainline HEAD SHA equals the merge commit; CI on main re-runs and is green; commit count and diff on main match the approved PR (no extra commits sneaked in).
Merge commit SHA, PR number, approvers, and CI run URL recorded in the PR and in the release notes/Confluence page, timestamped in UTC; branch-protection audit log retained.

Any override of branch protection (admin merge, bypassed check) requires a 'SDLC-Exception' Jira ticket, owner = Engineering Manager, with justification and 10-business-day review; logged in the exception register.
The immutable build artifact produced by CI from the merged mainline commit for this release; exactly one semantic-version tag applied to that commit and artifact.
At release cut for the current release train iteration; tag applied once the release candidate build is green.
Tag follows SemVer vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, is annotated (author, date, release notes), points to the exact release commit SHA, and matches the artifact version and container image tag in Artifactory.
Git tag SHA == release build commit SHA == artifact metadata version == image tag; all four reconcile with no mismatch before the tag is pushed.
Annotated tag, tagged commit SHA, CI build number, and generated changelog recorded in the release notes and Confluence, timestamped in UTC; tag is immutable (no re-tag).
If a tag must be corrected, delete-and-retag is prohibited; issue a new patch version and log a 'SDLC-Exception' Jira ticket, owner = Release Engineer, documenting the superseded tag.

Reusable CI/CD pipeline templates (build, test, SAST/SCA, package, deploy stages) covering the org's supported stacks (Java/Node/.NET), consumable by all delivery squads from the central pipeline-templates repo.
Current platform-enablement PI/quarter; templates versioned and published by end of the increment, then maintained on a rolling basis.

Each template defines required stages (build, unit test, coverage gate >=80% changed lines, SAST 0 critical/high, SCA, artifact publish, deploy) as reusable workflows with pinned action versions and documented inputs; no template ships without a README and example consumer.
Number of supported stacks == number of published templates; every template has at least one passing end-to-end pilot pipeline run recorded before publish.

Templates versioned via git tags in the pipeline-templates repo; release notes, example runs, and adoption guide stored in Confluence, timestamped; each version immutable and referenced by consumers via pinned ref.
Topology doc reflects the current release; refreshed on every schema/topology change and reviewed at least quarterly.

A squad needing to deviate from the standard template raises a 'SDLC-Exception' Jira ticket, owner = Engineering Manager, documenting the deviation and compensating controls; reviewed within 10 business days and logged.
All scheduled and event-driven pipeline runs in the orchestrator for the in-scope data/CI pipelines, monitored for run status, queue depth, and SLA-breach alerts in real time.
Continuous, 24x7, covering the current operational period; alert thresholds reviewed each release cycle.
Monitoring dashboard exposes per-pipeline: last run status, start/end time, duration vs SLA, queue depth, and error rate; alerts fire on failure or SLA breach with runbook link and on-call routing.
Expected vs actual run counts per schedule reconcile (missed runs = 0); records processed reconcile to source control totals within +/- 0% for critical feeds before downstream consumption.
Run history, alert events, and acknowledgements retained in the orchestrator and ITSM with UTC timestamps and run IDs; dashboards versioned; 90-day hot retention, 12-month archive.
SLA breach or failed run auto-creates a ServiceNow/Jira incident, routed to the on-call Data Engineer with severity by impact; unresolved P1 escalates to Platform Engineering Lead after 30 minutes.

Alert thresholds and SLA definitions are versioned in the monitoring-config repo and approved by the Platform Engineering Lead before activation; current version tagged and referenced by the dashboards.
Alerting sensitivity documented: warn at 80% of SLA duration, breach at 100%; queue-depth warn at >50 pending, critical at >200; tuned to keep false-positive rate < 5%.
Materiality: only pipelines feeding regulatory, financial, or customer-facing outputs are P1; internal/dev pipelines are P3, distinguished by a criticality tag in the CMDB/catalog.
All in-scope pipeline runs over a 7-day observation window; 100% of runs must appear on the dashboard with a status.
PASS = every scheduled run has a recorded status and every failure/SLA-breach generated an alert within 60 seconds; FAIL = any silent failure (run failed with no alert) or missing run status.
Silent failure or missed alert -> raise a P2 monitoring-gap incident, owner = Site Reliability Engineer, fix alert rule within 2 business days; log root cause in the incident record.
Monitoring/alert ruleset at the version tagged in the monitoring-config repo and approved for the current operational period.
SLA targets and thresholds sourced from the service catalog / data-product SLA definitions in the CMDB; no hard-coded values outside the config repo.
The current sprint plan and backlog status for the squad: committed stories, capacity, sprint goal, and burndown, published to all named stakeholders (Product Owner, Tech Lead, dependent squads).
The active sprint (e.g. Sprint 2026.07, 2-week iteration); plan published within 1 business day of sprint planning and refreshed at each daily standup.
Published plan shows for every committed story: title, estimate, assignee, status, and linkage to epic/PI objective; sprint goal and total committed vs capacity points are stated.
Sum of committed story points on the published plan equals the committed points in Jira Align for the sprint (delta = 0); story count on the shared view matches the Jira board.
Published plan snapshot (Jira Align dashboard link or exported PDF) stored in Confluence with sprint ID and UTC timestamp; each republish is versioned.
Scope changes after publish are tracked as scope-change entries in Jira Align with rationale and PO approval; late additions flagged in the next standup and re-published.
All committed sprint items in the published plan; 100% must be traceable to a Jira work item.
PASS = published plan reconciles to the Jira board (same items, estimates, statuses) and all stakeholders have access; FAIL = any committed item missing from the published view or points mismatch.
Discrepancy between published plan and board -> Scrum Master re-syncs and republishes within the same business day; recurring drift logged as a process defect in Jira.
Acceptance: plan published to all named stakeholders within 1 business day of planning, reconciles 1:1 with the Jira board, includes sprint goal and capacity.
Confluence 'Sprint Plans' space, page named 'Sprint <id> Plan' with the Jira Align dashboard embed and export attachment.
All backlog items in status Done or De-scoped/Won't-Do at sprint/PI close in Jira; archived with closure rationale to preserve the delivery audit trail.
End of each sprint and PI (current iteration); archival run within 2 business days of iteration close.

Each archived item carries: final status, closure rationale, resolver, closure date, and links to the delivering PR/release (for Done) or de-scope decision record (for de-scoped); items lacking rationale are not archivable.
Count of items eligible (Done + De-scoped at close) equals count archived (delta = 0); no eligible item remains in the active backlog after the archival run.

Archived items retain full Jira history (transitions, comments, links) and are moved to the archived project/board with iteration ID and UTC timestamp; export snapshot stored in the evidence repository.
An item flagged Done/de-scoped but missing rationale is held back and a 'closure-rationale-missing' Jira sub-task assigned to the item owner, resolved within 3 business days before archival.
Archival procedure version approved by the Scrum Master and documented in the team's Definition of Done; current version referenced in the runbook.
Sensitivity: archival is reversible for 30 days (items can be restored from the archived board) to guard against premature closure.
Materiality: items linked to regulatory or audit deliverables are retained per the record-retention schedule (7 years) even after archival; ordinary items follow the 12-month operational retention.
Retention driven by the enterprise records-retention policy; audit-relevant delivery records kept 7 years per internal SOX/records policy.
Archived audit-relevant items retained 7 years in the compliance evidence repository; operational items 12 months, then purged per policy.
N/A - no external regulatory filing deadline; internal SLA is archival within 2 business days of iteration close.
PASS = every archived item has final status + rationale + links and is retrievable from the archive; FAIL = any archived item missing rationale or not retrievable.
Missing-metadata or non-retrievable archive -> restore item, complete metadata, re-archive; log gap in the archival-quality checklist owned by the Scrum Master.
Jira field definitions: status, resolution, resolution-date, and the custom 'closure-rationale' field, as defined in the Jira project schema.
Backlog item counts by status from the Jira board at iteration close serve as the archival control totals.

The developer-experience / engineering-metrics dashboard covering DORA metrics (deployment frequency, lead time, change-fail rate, MTTR) plus DevEx signals (build time, PR cycle time, flaky-test rate) across all delivery squads.
Rolling trailing 90 days with weekly refresh; dashboard live for the current quarter.

Each metric has a documented definition, source system, calculation, and refresh cadence; dashboard shows current value, trend, and target for every metric; no metric renders without a defined source query.
Dashboard metric values reconcile to the underlying source (CI/CD logs, Jira) within +/- 1%; deployment count on the dashboard equals the deployment count in the pipeline audit log for the period.

Dashboard definition (queries, data model) versioned in the analytics repo; published dashboard URL and a period snapshot stored in Confluence with UTC timestamp; metric-definition changes are versioned.

Metric data gaps or source outages are flagged on the dashboard with a data-quality banner and logged as a Jira data-quality ticket, owner = Platform Engineering Lead, resolved within 3 business days.
Metric definitions (DORA + DevEx) approved by the Platform Engineering Lead and versioned in the metrics-catalog repo; dashboard references the approved definition version.
Sensitivity: metrics are reported at team/aggregate level only; no individual-developer ranking, to avoid gaming and preserve psychological safety.
Materiality: DORA metrics and change-fail rate are primary KPIs reviewed by leadership; secondary DevEx signals are informational and not gated.
Decision to publish and the target thresholds for each metric documented in the Confluence dashboard charter, approved by the Platform Engineering Lead.
Recipients: all engineering squads, Tech Leads, and Engineering Management; dashboard link distributed via the engineering Teams channel and the internal metrics portal.
All metrics on the published dashboard for the trailing 90-day window; 100% validated against source.

PASS = every metric has a defined source and reconciles to source within +/- 1%, dashboard loads under 5 seconds, and is accessible to all stakeholders; FAIL = any unsourced metric or reconciliation variance > 1%.
Reconciliation variance > 1% -> data-quality ticket to the Platform Engineering Lead, dashboard flagged, root cause fixed within 3 business days before the metric is treated as authoritative.
Acceptance: dashboard live, all metrics sourced and reconciled to +/-1%, loads < 5s, accessible to all engineering stakeholders, definitions documented.
BI/reporting platform workspace 'Engineering DevEx Metrics'; definitions and snapshots in Confluence 'DevEx Metrics' space.
Developer satisfaction (DevSat/eNPS) scores collected from all engineers in the delivery organization via the quarterly DevEx survey; anonymized responses only.
Quarterly survey window for the current quarter (2-week collection period); trend compared to prior quarters.
Each response records: anonymized respondent token, squad, survey question scores (1-5 Likert), and free-text; responses missing required Likert items are excluded from the score calculation.
Responses received reconcile to invitations sent for response-rate calc; target response rate >= 60% of engineers; score is computed only over completed responses.
Raw anonymized responses and computed scores exported and stored in the data warehouse and Confluence with survey ID and UTC timestamp; PII-free; retained 24 months for trend analysis.
Squads with response rate < 60% are flagged and re-surveyed once; incomplete/duplicate submissions excluded and logged in the survey-quality note owned by the Platform Engineering Lead.
Survey instrument and scoring methodology (question set, Likert scale, eNPS formula) approved by the Platform Engineering Lead and versioned; current version referenced on the survey.
Sensitivity: results reported only at squad/org aggregate with minimum n=5 responses per group to protect anonymity; groups below threshold rolled up.
Materiality: overall DevSat/eNPS and quarter-over-quarter delta are the headline metrics driving platform investment; per-question scores are diagnostic only.
All completed survey responses for the current quarter; 100% of valid responses included in the score.
PASS = response rate >= 60%, anonymity preserved (no group below n=5 shown), and scores computed per the approved methodology; FAIL = response rate < 60% or any identifiable small-group reporting.
Response rate < 60% -> extend/re-run collection once, owner = Platform Engineering Lead; if still short, report with a low-confidence caveat and log in the survey-quality note.
Survey schema field definitions: respondent token (anonymized), squad, per-question Likert score, eNPS category, free-text; defined in the survey-tool export spec.
Invitations sent and responses received counts from the survey tool serve as control totals for response-rate reconciliation.
Developer feedback items from the DevEx survey, retros, and platform support tickets, triaged and converted into prioritized backlog items in the platform-improvement backlog.
Current platform improvement cycle (per PI/quarter); feedback actioned into the backlog within 2 weeks of the survey/retro close.

Each actioned feedback theme becomes a Jira item with: source reference, problem statement, priority, owner, and target increment; feedback items are tagged 'devex-feedback' and linked back to the originating survey/retro.
Count of triaged feedback themes reconciles to backlog items created or explicitly declined-with-reason (delta = 0); no theme left untriaged after the cycle.
Feedback-to-backlog mapping (theme -> Jira key or decline rationale) recorded in Confluence with cycle ID and UTC timestamp; backlog items retain the source link; retained 12 months.
Feedback themes not actioned are logged with a documented decline rationale and communicated back to developers; disputed declines escalate to the Platform Engineering Lead for review.
Triage/prioritization method (impact x reach scoring) approved by the Platform Engineering Lead and documented in the platform backlog policy; current version referenced during triage.
Sensitivity: prioritization scores are recalculated when new feedback volume shifts reach estimates; high-impact/high-reach items promoted into the next increment.
Materiality: only themes affecting >=3 squads or a top-3 DevEx pain point are candidates for the current increment; smaller items parked in the backlog with a tag.
All triaged feedback themes for the cycle; 100% must resolve to a backlog item or a documented decline.

PASS = every feedback theme has a Jira item or decline rationale, each carries a source link, and top themes are scheduled into the increment; FAIL = any untriaged theme or backlog item lacking a source link.
Untriaged or unlinked feedback -> Platform Engineering Lead completes triage in the next backlog refinement; recurring gaps logged as a process defect.
Feedback record fields: source, theme, affected squads, impact score, reach score, priority, linked Jira key; defined in the platform backlog schema.
Total feedback themes ingested vs themes triaged serve as control totals for the reconciliation.

All engineering documentation pages in the Confluence 'Engineering Knowledge Base' space (and READMEs in the GitHub Enterprise 'platform-*' repos) whose 'Last reviewed' label is older than 12 months OR whose subject component has been decommissioned per the CMDB. Scope excludes regulatory/actuarial governance docs held in the model governance repository.
Documents last modified on or before 2025-06-30 (rolling 12-month lookback); archival run executed the first business week of each quarter.

Each archived page carries a 'Status: Archived' banner, a sunset date, and a link to the current replacement page (or 'No replacement - capability retired, CMDB CI xxxxx'). Pages missing a replacement reference are blocked from archival.
Count of pages moved to the 'Archive' space in Confluence equals the count on the archival worklist exported from the Jira epic; delta must be 0 before the run is marked complete.
Confluence page-version history plus the exported archival worklist CSV (with page ID, sunset date, replacement URL, archiver, ISO-8601 timestamp) attached to the Jira story and retained 3 years.

Any doc that cannot be archived (still linked from a live runbook, no owner, or replacement not yet published) is logged as a sub-task on the Jira epic with disposition 'Deferred - reason', owner = Backend Developer, 10-business-day resolution SLA.
Sample of 25 pages from the archival worklist plus a full sweep for any page still tagged 'current' but last reviewed > 12 months ago.

PASS = 100% of sampled archived pages have Archived banner + sunset date + valid replacement link, and 0 stale 'current' pages remain; FAIL if any archived page lacks a replacement reference or any stale current page is found.
Failures reopen the Jira story, assigned to Software Engineer with a 5-business-day fix SLA; recurrence > 2 quarters escalates to the Engineering Manager for a knowledge-management process review.
Confluence page metadata fields used: page ID, space key, 'Last reviewed' label, 'Owner' property, and the linked CMDB CI status (Active/Retired) that drives the sunset decision.
Reconcile total live+archived page count in the Engineering KB space before and after the run against the CMDB component inventory; no net loss of content, only status transitions.

The change/release under review at the implementation gate: all pull requests targeting the release branch in GitHub Enterprise for the named Jira release version, together with the ADR(s) and design package attached to the Jira 'Design Gate' issue.
Gate decision applies to the current release cycle (2-week sprint / named release version); approval expires if the release is not deployed within 30 calendar days and must be re-granted.

Gate record captures: ADR link, design-vs-implementation conformance note, CI status (green), SAST/SCA status (0 critical/high), and named approver. All fields mandatory before the Jira gate transition is permitted.
Number of PRs merged to the release branch equals the number listed on the design package's scope table; any unlisted PR blocks approval until reconciled.
Signed gate decision recorded as a comment on the Jira 'Design Gate' issue with the approver's name, decision (Approve/Reject/Conditional), conditions, and ISO-8601 timestamp; retained 3 years.
Conditional approvals log each condition as a linked Jira sub-task with owner and due date; unresolved conditions at deploy time block promotion via the pipeline gate.

All production Kafka topics and consumer groups in the streaming pipeline that feed the Enterprise data warehouse/lakehouse landing zone, plus the Flink/Spark Structured Streaming jobs that read them.
Continuous, 24x7 real-time monitoring; dashboards retain 90 days of metric history and alerts evaluate on 1-minute windows.
Every topic exposes consumer-lag, partition-skew, and end-to-end latency series to Prometheus; a topic missing any of the three required metrics is flagged red on the pipeline health dashboard.
Records produced to source topics reconcile with records landed in the lakehouse per 15-minute bucket within a 0.1% tolerance; sustained breach raises a P2 alert.

Grafana dashboard JSON is versioned in the source code/CI-CD repository; alert-firing history and on-call acknowledgements are retained in the alerting platform for 90 days and exported to the ITSM incident record.
Each threshold breach auto-creates a ServiceNow incident tagged 'streaming-pipeline'; disposition (resolved / false-positive / suppressed-with-reason) recorded on the incident before closure.
All in-scope topics/consumer groups over a representative peak-load window (e.g., the daily batch-catch-up spike) plus a synthetic lag-injection test on one non-prod topic.

PASS = consumer lag < 10,000 messages sustained, p99 end-to-end latency < 5s, and 0 partitions in a stalled state; FAIL if any metric exceeds threshold for > 5 consecutive minutes without a firing alert.

On alert, on-call SRE follows the linked runbook; if lag is unrecoverable within the 30-minute SLA, escalate to Software Engineer (owner) and open a P1 in ServiceNow with the consumer-group offset snapshot attached.

Acceptance: telemetry is 'observable' when lag, partition utilization, and end-to-end latency for every prod topic are live on the Grafana dashboard with at least one bound alert rule each and a 90-day retention window.
Grafana dashboard 'Streaming Pipeline Health' (folder: Data Engineering); alert rules and dashboard JSON stored at repo path /observability/streaming/ in the source code/CI-CD repository.
Every producer, topic, stream-processing job, and sink in the streaming pipeline within the named domain; documentation covers event flow, partitioning keys, schemas, and consumer groups.

Topology doc includes, per topic: name, partition count, key strategy, producing service, consuming groups, schema subject, and retention. A topic present in the broker but absent from the doc fails the completeness check.
Topic count in the documented topology equals the live topic count from the Kafka admin API (excluding internal __consumer_offsets); delta must be 0.

Topology doc lives as a versioned Confluence page and a source-controlled diagram (Mermaid/C4) at /docs/streaming/topology in the source code/CI-CD repository, each carrying a version and last-updated timestamp.
Undocumented or orphaned topics discovered during reconciliation are logged as Jira tasks with disposition 'document' or 'decommission', owner = Backend Developer, 10-business-day SLA.
All prod topics and stream jobs in the domain, compared against the live broker/topic inventory.
PASS = 100% of live topics documented with all required fields and diagram reflects actual producer/consumer wiring; FAIL if any live topic is missing or a documented edge does not match runtime.
Discrepancies open a Jira 'doc-drift' task assigned to Software Engineer, 5-business-day fix SLA; the topology page is blocked from 'Approved' until drift = 0.

Field definitions sourced from the schema registry subjects (Avro/Protobuf) and the Kafka topic configs (partitions, retention, cleanup.policy); the doc references subject names and versions, not copied field lists.
Reconcile documented topic/partition totals against the Kafka admin API describe-topics output; totals must match exactly.

All schema-registry subjects (Avro/Protobuf/JSON Schema) backing the streaming pipeline's topics for the named domain, plus their compatibility modes and versions surfaced into the data catalog/quality tool.
Registry entries kept current continuously; a subject registration/promotion is required for every producer schema change and reconciled to the catalog daily.

Every active topic has a registered subject with owner, description, compatibility mode, and business-glossary link populated in the catalog; a topic with data but no registered subject is a hard failure.
Count of registered subjects reconciles with count of active prod topics (1:key + 1:value where applicable); unmatched subjects/topics are listed for remediation, target delta 0.
Schema definitions are versioned in the source code/CI-CD repository (schemas/ path) and auto-published to the registry by the pipeline; catalog sync run logs are retained 12 months with timestamps.
Subjects failing catalog discoverability rules (missing owner/description) are logged in the data catalog/quality tool's issue queue, owner = Backend Developer, remediation within 10 business days.
All active subjects in the schema registry compared against active topics and against catalog entries.
PASS = 100% of active topics have a current, catalog-discoverable subject with required metadata and a set compatibility mode; FAIL if any subject is orphaned, stale, or missing mandatory metadata.

Failed subjects create a data-quality issue routed to Software Engineer; if a breaking schema change was published without notice, roll back the subject and open an SDLC-Exception ticket, 10-business-day remediation.
Field definitions come from the schema registry subject definitions (field names, types, doc strings) and the catalog's technical metadata; not re-typed by hand.
Reconcile registry subject count vs catalog dataset count for the domain; totals must match, with orphans reported to 0.

The full scope of the named release: all user stories/defects in the release version, the impacted services/components per the change record, and the risk-ranked feature list requiring functional, integration, regression, performance, and UAT coverage.
Plan governs the current release cycle; authored at sprint/release planning and re-approved if release scope changes materially.

Plan states, per risk area: test types, entry/exit criteria, environments, test-data source, coverage target (>= 80% line, >= 90% on critical paths), and defect-severity gate. A high-risk feature without an assigned test type fails plan review.
Every in-scope story/defect maps to at least one planned test case; traceability matrix shows 0 orphan requirements and 0 orphan test cases.
Approved test plan and traceability matrix stored on the Jira release version and Confluence 'Test Plan' page, version-stamped and timestamped; retained per release records policy.
Scope items deferred out of test coverage are logged with a risk-acceptance note and named approver on the Jira release; unresolved coverage gaps block plan approval.
Test strategy version is approved and recorded on the Confluence Test Plan page header; changes require re-approval by the Test Lead and Tech Lead before execution begins.

Risk-based sensitivity: features rated High risk require regression + integration + performance coverage; Medium require regression + integration; Low require regression. Thresholds documented in the plan's risk table.
Materiality gate: no Critical or High-severity open defects at release; up to 5 Medium defects allowed with documented workarounds and Product Owner sign-off.
All in-scope requirements and their mapped test cases in the traceability matrix for the release.
PASS = 100% of in-scope requirements traced to >= 1 test case, coverage targets set, and defect gate defined; FAIL if any requirement is untested or exit criteria are absent.
Gaps found in review reopen the plan for the Software Engineer/Test Lead, 3-business-day SLA; unresolved gaps escalate to the Release Manager and block the release gate.
Acceptance: plan is approved when the traceability matrix is complete, coverage and defect-severity gates are set, environments/test-data are named, and Test Lead + Tech Lead have signed off.
Approved plan on Confluence 'Release <version> Test Plan'; traceability matrix and approvals on the Jira release version; both linked from the release runbook.

The named stream-processing job(s) requiring exactly-once semantics and late-arrival (watermark/allowed-lateness) handling: source topics, checkpointing config, transactional sink(s), and the windowing operators.
Configuration validated for the current release and re-validated on any change to sink, checkpoint interval, or watermark policy.

Job config sets processing.guarantee=exactly_once (or Flink checkpointing EXACTLY_ONCE) with a transactional/idempotent sink, defined watermark strategy, and allowed-lateness window. Missing any of these is a config failure caught in CI.

Under a duplicate-injection test, output record count equals distinct input event count (0 duplicates); under a delayed-event test, late events within the allowed-lateness window are counted and beyond it are routed to the side-output/DLQ.
Config-as-code committed to the source code/CI-CD repository with PR history; the exactly-once/late-arrival test report is attached to the merge and retained 12 months.
Events arriving beyond allowed lateness are written to a dead-letter/side-output topic and logged; a reconciliation job reports DLQ volume, disposition tracked in ServiceNow.
The QA test environments to be provisioned for the release: SIT and UAT tiers, their compute/data stores, seeded masked test data, integration stubs/live endpoints, and access for the test team.
Environments provisioned for the current release test window; refreshed each release and torn down or reset after UAT sign-off.

Each environment provisioned from version-controlled IaC, config parity with production validated, masked test data loaded, and a post-provision smoke test passing. An environment failing smoke test is not released to QA.
Provisioned resource inventory matches the IaC plan output (terraform plan shows 0 drift); seeded test-record counts match the expected dataset manifest.
IaC state, terraform plan/apply logs, and the smoke-test report are stored in the source code/CI-CD repository and linked to the ServiceNow change ticket, timestamped and retained 12 months.
Provisioning failures or config drift are logged on the ServiceNow change ticket with disposition; environment blocked from QA use until drift = 0, owner = Software Engineer, 3-business-day SLA.
All environments provisioned for the release (SIT, UAT) and their seeded datasets and integration endpoints.
PASS = terraform plan shows 0 drift vs prod-parity baseline, smoke test green, and masked test data loaded to expected counts; FAIL on any drift, failed smoke test, or unmasked PII detected.
Failed provisioning reopens the change task for Software Engineer; if unmasked PII is detected, halt, purge the dataset, and open an SDLC-Exception ticket with a 24-hour remediation SLA.
Environment/config field definitions come from the IaC variable files and the CMDB environment CI records (tier, region, sizing), referenced not duplicated.
Reconcile provisioned resource counts and seeded record counts against the IaC plan and dataset manifest; both must match with 0 drift.
All UAT scenarios for the release, mapped to business acceptance criteria, executed by named business stakeholders in the UAT environment; scope = every in-scope story requiring business validation.
UAT executed during the release UAT window (typically the final sprint before go-live); sign-off valid for the specific release version only.
Each UAT case records: scenario, tester, execution date, actual vs expected result, pass/fail, and linked defect if failed. A case with no recorded outcome fails the UAT completeness check.
Executed UAT case count equals planned UAT case count in the traceability matrix; unexecuted cases must be 0 or explicitly waived with business sign-off before closure.
UAT results, defects, and the signed acceptance form are captured on the Jira release version and Confluence UAT page, timestamped and version-stamped; retained per release records policy.
Failed UAT cases raise Jira defects with severity; Critical/High block sign-off; Medium/Low may be deferred with a Product Owner-approved risk note and target release.
All planned UAT scenarios for the release executed by business stakeholders in the UAT environment.
PASS = 100% of UAT cases executed with recorded outcomes and 0 open Critical/High defects; FAIL if any case is unexecuted or a Critical/High defect remains open at sign-off.
Failed cases reopen for the QA Analyst and dev team; blocking defects escalate to the Product Owner and Release Manager and hold the go-live gate until resolved or formally risk-accepted.
UAT expected-result definitions trace to the story acceptance criteria in Jira; testers validate against those criteria, not free interpretation.
Reconcile executed vs planned UAT case counts and pass/fail tallies in the traceability matrix; executed must equal planned (minus signed waivers).

All critical integration points and data flows for the release in staging: Guidewire PolicyCenter/ClaimCenter/BillingCenter interfaces, partner APIs, ESB/Kafka flows, and downstream lakehouse loads exercised end-to-end.
Integration tests run in staging for the current release candidate; re-run on every deploy to staging until the release is promoted.

Each integration point has a contract test and an end-to-end data-flow test; request/response schemas validate, and payload field mappings match the interface spec. An untested critical interface fails the gate.
Records sent across each interface reconcile with records received downstream (e.g., policies bound in PolicyCenter equal rows landed in the lakehouse) within a 0% tolerance for critical flows.

Integration test run reports (pass/fail per interface), reconciliation output, and pipeline logs stored in the source code/CI-CD repository and linked to the compliance evidence repository; retained 12 months.
Failed interfaces raise Jira defects and block promotion; transient failures are retried once, persistent failures escalate to Integration Engineer, 3-business-day SLA, tracked on the change ticket.
Interface test approach/version is approved and recorded on the staging test plan; changes to contracts require re-approval by the Integration Architect before re-test.
Latency/throughput sensitivity documented per interface: p99 response time and max sustained TPS thresholds; breach flags a performance risk before promotion.
Materiality: any reconciliation discrepancy on a financial/policy-of-record flow is material and blocks release; non-critical reporting flows tolerate <= 0.1% variance with a logged note.
All critical integration points and their end-to-end data flows in the staging environment for the release.
PASS = 100% of critical interfaces pass contract + e2e tests and reconcile with 0 discrepancy on financial/PoR flows; FAIL on any contract break, failed e2e flow, or reconciliation mismatch.

Failures reopen for Integration Engineer/Software Engineer; unresolved critical failures escalate to the Release Manager and hold the promotion gate; an SDLC-Exception ticket is required to proceed with a known non-critical failure.
Acceptance: staging integration testing passes when every critical interface passes contract + end-to-end tests, reconciliation is clean on critical flows, and performance thresholds are met.
Test reports and reconciliation output on the CI run and the staging test plan; audit evidence copied to the compliance evidence repository and linked from the change ticket.
Pre/post comparison: downstream data state before and after the release flows is diffed; only intended changes appear, with row-count and key-field reconciliation passing.
The ServiceNow change ticket (CHG#) authorizing the staging deploy is linked in the CI run and the test report; test evidence is attached to that change record before promotion approval.

All end-to-end user journeys tagged @e2e in the acceptance-criteria suite for the release epic (Jira epic in project SWE); scope = every user story in the sprint marked 'Ready for QA', covering happy-path plus 2 negative paths per story.
Current sprint window (2-week cadence); E2E run executes on every merge to the develop branch and as a gate before promotion to the staging/UAT environment.
Every acceptance criterion in each user story maps to at least one Playwright/Cypress E2E spec; test IDs referenced back to the Jira story key; no story marked Done with an unmapped criterion.
E2E pass rate = 100% of critical-path flows and >=98% of full suite green; flaky-test quarantine <=2% of specs; run duration under 15 minutes on the CI runner.
CI run artifact (JUnit XML + video/trace on failure) retained 90 days in GitHub Actions, tagged with commit SHA, build number, and dev-environment version; results posted to the PR check.

Each failing flow opens a Jira bug linked to the story with severity; blocking bugs stop promotion; non-blocking logged with owner and target sprint; flaky specs get a 'flaky' label and 5-day fix SLA.
All 'Ready for QA' stories in the sprint; sampled against seeded synthetic test data covering policy/claims/billing personas in Guidewire dev.
Pass = every acceptance criterion assertion green; fail = any critical-path assertion red or E2E suite green rate <98%; regression = any previously-passing flow now failing.

On failure, auto-create Jira bug type 'Defect', assign to owning developer; deployment gate remains red until fixed or waived via 'SDLC-Exception' ticket owned by Engineering Manager with 10-business-day remediation SLA.
Acceptance criteria written in Gherkin Given/When/Then on each Jira story, reviewed by Product Owner and Tech Lead before development starts; Definition of Done requires all criteria automated.
GitHub Actions run summary + Allure/HTML report attached to the PR and archived in the ITSM change record (ServiceNow/Jira) for the release; linked from the epic.

Scope = all internal shared libraries, platform components, and services published to the inner-source org in the source-code/CI-CD repository; population = every repo tagged 'inner-source' with a published CONTRIBUTING.md and codeowners file.
Program runs continuously; contribution metrics and reuse rollups reported quarterly to the Platform Engineering Lead.

Each inner-source repo has: README with setup/run/test/deploy, CONTRIBUTING.md, CODEOWNERS, license/usage terms, and a maintainer contact; validated by a repo-scorecard CI check that fails below 100% of required files.

Reported reuse count reconciles: number of downstream repos declaring the shared package as a dependency (from the package registry / SBOM scan) matches the reuse figure in the quarterly program report within +/-2%.
Quarterly program report (contributions, reuse, maintainer response times) stored in Confluence with version/date; snapshot of CI scorecard results retained 12 months.

Repos missing required governance files logged as Jira tasks against the owning team with a 30-day fix window; repos with no maintainer response >10 business days flagged for reassignment via 'SDLC-Exception' ticket owned by Engineering Manager.
Sample of 10 inner-source repos per quarter plus all repos with >5 external contributions, checked for governance completeness and PR review adherence.
Pass = repo scorecard 100% required files present and mean maintainer first-response <2 business days; fail = any required file missing or response >10 business days.
Non-compliant repos get a remediation Jira task (30-day SLA); persistent non-compliance escalates to Platform Engineering Lead and may result in de-listing from the inner-source catalog.
Inner-source program charter v-current, approved by Platform Engineering Lead; contribution model (fork-and-PR with trusted-committer review) documented in Confluence.
Reuse and contribution metrics sourced from the source-code/CI-CD repository API and package-registry dependency graph; no manual spreadsheet counts.

Scope = synthetic test data sets for every in-scope QA suite of the release: policy, claims, and billing scenarios in Guidewire dev/QA, plus edge/boundary and negative-path records; no production PII copied into non-prod.
Refreshed each sprint before QA execution and re-masked on every non-prod environment refresh from production.

Every required field for each test scenario is populated with valid, referentially-consistent values (policy->claim->billing FKs intact); all direct identifiers masked/synthesized; data validated against source schema definitions before load.
Row counts per entity in the test set reconcile to the planned scenario matrix (expected vs loaded within +/-0); referential-integrity check returns 0 orphaned records.

Test-data generation script + manifest (dataset version, seed, row counts, masking rules) committed to the source-code repo and tagged; a copy of the load log retained 90 days with timestamp in the ITSM record.

Records failing validation or masking are quarantined and logged in Jira; any need to use production-derived data requires a 'SDLC-Exception' ticket owned by the Data Governance Lead with DPO sign-off.
The full generated test-data set for the sprint plus a 5% sample manually inspected for realism and masking effectiveness.
Pass = 100% required fields valid, 0 unmasked direct identifiers detected by the PII scanner, 0 referential-integrity violations; fail = any unmasked PII or >0 orphaned records.

PII-scanner hits block the dataset from promotion; the record set is regenerated; exception to ship partial data requires 'SDLC-Exception' ticket owned by Engineering Manager, 5-business-day remediation SLA.
Field definitions taken from the Guidewire policy/claims/billing data dictionary and the data catalog/quality tool; each generated field maps to a cataloged source column with type and constraints.
Control totals (record counts per entity, sum of key numeric fields) captured from the scenario matrix and compared to loaded totals in the test warehouse; variance must be 0.

Scope = the candidate capability/epic under discovery; assess feasibility across the affected systems (Guidewire policy/claims/billing, integration layer, data platform) named in the epic's architecture context in Jira.
Discovery/elaboration phase for the epic, completed before the epic enters a sprint (typically 1-2 sprints ahead).

Feasibility record captures: affected systems/CMDB CIs, integration points, estimated complexity (T-shirt or story-point range), key technical risks, and required non-functional constraints; no field left as TBD before ARB review.
Every dependency/system named in the feasibility note reconciles to a CMDB CI or a documented external service; count of named systems = count of linked CIs.
Feasibility findings recorded as an ADR + spike report attached to the epic in Jira, versioned with author and date; retained for the life of the initiative.
Open technical risks logged as Jira risk items with owner and mitigation; any 'not feasible as scoped' finding routes back to Product Owner for re-scoping via a documented decision.
Estimation/complexity methodology (reference-class story pointing + risk-adjusted T-shirt sizing) documented and approved by the Tech Lead; version noted on the feasibility record.
Sensitivity: if effort estimate varies >30% under best/worst-case assumptions, the epic is flagged high-uncertainty and requires a de-risking spike before commitment.
Materiality: initiatives estimated above 20 story points or touching >=2 core systems require formal ARB review before build.
All feasibility records produced this quarter for epics entering the backlog; sampled for completeness and dependency accuracy.
Pass = feasibility record complete (all mandatory sections), dependencies reconciled to CMDB, and ARB/Tech Lead sign-off present; fail = missing sections or unlinked dependencies.

Incomplete feasibility routes the epic back to discovery; proceeding to build without sign-off requires a 'SDLC-Exception' ticket owned by the Engineering Manager with 10-business-day remediation SLA.
Acceptance = documented feasibility verdict (feasible / feasible-with-conditions / not-feasible), complexity range, risk list, and dependency map, reviewed by Tech Lead and (where material) ARB.
ADR + spike report stored in the epic's Jira/Confluence space; ARB decision recorded in the architecture governance register.

Scope = all upstream/downstream dependencies for the capability: internal systems (Guidewire modules, integration layer, data platform), other delivery teams, and external/vendor services; population = every integration point in the epic's context diagram.
Elaboration phase before the epic is committed to a sprint; dependency list re-validated at sprint planning.
Each dependency entry records: system/team name, CMDB CI id, interface (API/event/file), direction, owner/contact, and readiness status; no entry missing an owner or CI reference.
Every named system dependency reconciles to a CMDB CI (count of dependencies = count of resolved CIs); cross-team dependencies each have a matching Jira link on both boards.
Dependency register maintained as a Confluence/Jira table attached to the epic, versioned with date and author; snapshot retained for the life of the initiative.

Unresolved or blocked dependencies logged as Jira 'Dependency' items with owner and target date; cross-team blockers escalated at scrum-of-scrums; unowned dependencies flagged for the Integration Architect.
Dependency-mapping approach (context diagram + CMDB traversal + interface catalog review) documented and approved by the Integration Architect; version noted on the register.
Sensitivity: any single external/vendor dependency on the critical path triggers a contingency/fallback plan requirement before commitment.
Materiality: dependencies that would delay the epic by >1 sprint if unmet are marked critical and reviewed at portfolio level.
Post-implementation, the realized integration set is compared to the pre-build dependency register; any integration built but not in the register is back-filled and reviewed.
Each production integration change links to a ServiceNow/Jira change ticket referencing the dependency register entry it satisfies.
The full dependency register for the epic plus a cross-check of critical dependencies against the affected teams' backlogs.
Pass = 100% of dependencies have owner + CMDB CI + readiness status and all critical ones have a matched commitment; fail = any unowned/unlinked dependency or unconfirmed critical dependency.

Unresolved critical dependencies block sprint commitment; proceeding at risk requires a 'SDLC-Exception' ticket owned by the Engineering Manager with a documented mitigation and 10-business-day review.
Acceptance = complete, owner-attributed dependency register with readiness status and critical-path flags, reviewed by the Integration Architect and Tech Lead.
Dependency register + context diagram stored in the epic's Confluence page; CMDB relationships updated; cross-team links recorded on respective Jira boards.
Scope = the team's product backlog in Jira for the value stream; population = all 'Ready' and 'Refined' backlog items (epics/stories/spikes) eligible for the next 2-3 sprints.
Re-ranked every sprint at backlog refinement and again immediately before sprint planning (2-week cadence).

Every ranked item has: value/priority score (e.g. WSJF components), risk rating, estimate, dependency links, and a rank order with no ties in the top 20; unestimated items are excluded from the ranked zone.
Count of items in the prioritized backlog view equals the count of 'Ready/Refined' items in Jira (no dropped or duplicated stories); rank is a strict total order over the top slice.
Ranked backlog snapshot exported from Jira after each refinement, dated and versioned, attached to the sprint page in Confluence; WSJF scoring sheet retained.
Items that cannot be ranked (missing estimate, unclear value, blocked by dependency) moved to a 'Needs Refinement' status with owner and reason logged; escalated if blocking for >1 sprint.

Scope = all engineering teams in the value stream; survey population = every active developer (IC and lead) with >=1 sprint tenure; toolchain areas covered: local dev, CI/CD, code review, testing, environments, and release.
Survey window = 2-week collection period; run quarterly with a lightweight monthly pulse on the top-2 friction areas.
Each survey response has required fields: team, role, friction area, severity (1-5), and free-text example; incomplete or anonymous-but-unscored responses excluded from the quantitative rollup.
All defined topics and schemas in the design; peer design review with a Data Architect and the consuming teams.
Response count reconciles: respondents / invited engineers >=60% for the result to be considered representative; per-team counts sum to the total.
Anonymized survey results, ranked friction list, and analysis deck stored in the BI/reporting platform and Confluence, dated and versioned; raw responses retained per privacy policy.
Low response rate (<60%) triggers a reminder and extension; unresolved top-5 friction items become DevEx backlog Jira items with owner and target quarter.
All submitted survey responses for the quarter plus DORA/DevEx metrics (lead time, deployment frequency, build time) as corroborating quantitative evidence.
Pass = >=60% response rate and a ranked friction list produced with the top-5 items assigned owners; fail = response rate <60% or no actionable findings captured.
Findings without a clear owner are escalated to the Platform Engineering Lead; disputed severity resolved by triangulating with DORA metrics before prioritization.
Acceptance = a ranked, evidence-backed friction list with severity and affected teams, reviewed by the Platform Engineering Lead and fed into the DevEx backlog.
Survey report + ranked findings + metric appendix stored in the BI/reporting platform dashboard and linked from the DevEx Confluence space.

Scope = SAST over all first-party source in the release repos and DAST over the deployed application in the staging environment; SCA over all third-party dependencies; population = every service/repo in the release train plus running endpoints exposed by the app.
SAST + SCA run on every pull request and nightly; DAST run each release candidate before promotion to production; full authenticated DAST at least monthly.
Each finding record has: rule id/CWE, severity (CVSS), file/endpoint location, status, and remediation owner; scan configs (rulesets, DAST scope, auth) version-controlled and current.
Findings reconcile between the scanner dashboard and the tracking backlog: 100% of open critical/high findings have a matching Jira ticket; counts match within +/-0.

SAST/DAST/SCA reports (SARIF + HTML) retained 12 months in the security ticketing/evidence repository, tagged with commit SHA, scan config version, and timestamp; attached to the release change record.

Each true-positive opens a security Jira ticket with severity SLA (critical 7 days, high 30, medium 90); false positives suppressed with justification in the tool; risk acceptances via 'SDLC-Exception' ticket approved by the CISO/Application Security Lead.
All release repos (SAST/SCA) and all externally-reachable endpoints in staging (DAST); sampled with a known-vulnerable canary to confirm detection.
Release gate: 0 critical/high SAST or SCA findings unaddressed; <=5 medium permitted only with approved waivers; DAST returns no unremediated high-risk issues; fail = any un-waived critical/high.

Un-waived critical/high blocks promotion via the CI security gate; remediation tracked to SLA; exceptions require 'SDLC-Exception' ticket owned by the Application Security Lead with CISO co-sign and a dated remediation plan.
Acceptance = scans executed with current rulesets on the full scope, all critical/high triaged, and the security quality gate green (or all exceptions formally approved) before release.
Scan results and gate status attached to the PR checks and the release change ticket in the ITSM/security ticketing system; SARIF stored in the compliance evidence repository.
Scope = all epics accepted into the value stream backlog for the upcoming PI/quarter; population = each epic to be decomposed into INVEST-compliant, sprint-sized user stories in Jira.

Each story has: title, description, Gherkin acceptance criteria, estimate <=8 points, parent epic link, and a Definition-of-Ready checklist passed; stories >8 points are split further before entering a sprint.
Sum of decomposed story scope traces back to the parent epic (no orphan stories, no epic scope left uncovered); count of stories per epic recorded and reconciled at refinement.
Story breakdown captured in Jira with epic links and a refinement timestamp; refinement notes stored in Confluence, versioned by session date.
Stories failing Definition-of-Ready held in 'Needs Refinement' with the gap logged; oversized or ambiguous stories flagged for a spike; unresolved after 2 refinements escalated to the Product Owner.
Decomposition method = INVEST + story-splitting patterns (workflow steps, business rules, happy/unhappy path), documented in the team working agreement and approved by the Scrum Master.
Sensitivity: any story still estimated >8 points after splitting is treated as high-uncertainty and requires a spike or further decomposition before commitment.
Materiality: epics spanning >3 sprints of stories are reviewed with the Product Owner for possible re-scoping or MVP slicing.
All stories decomposed for the upcoming PI, sampled for INVEST compliance and acceptance-criteria completeness.
Pass = 100% of sprint-bound stories <=8 points with Gherkin acceptance criteria and a linked epic; fail = any story oversized, missing criteria, or orphaned.
Non-ready stories are excluded from sprint planning; committing a non-ready story requires Scrum Master + Product Owner sign-off recorded on the story.
Acceptance = a set of INVEST-compliant, estimated, criteria-bearing stories that fully cover each parent epic, reviewed at refinement by the team and Product Owner.
Decomposed stories live in the Jira backlog under their epics; refinement outcomes recorded in the sprint/PI Confluence page.
Scope = unit tests for all new and changed code paths in the pull request; population = every changed public method and branch in the diff for the service/repo under change.
Authored with the code change; executed on every commit locally and on every pull request in CI; coverage gate evaluated per PR.
Each test has clear arrange/act/assert, meaningful name, and asserts behavior not implementation; no changed public method left untested; tests deterministic (no reliance on wall-clock/network).
Coverage reconciles: line coverage >=80% overall and >=90% on critical paths; coverage on changed lines >=80% (enforced by the PR coverage diff); test count increases with new public methods.
JUnit/coverage (Cobertura/LCOV) reports published as CI artifacts retained 90 days, tagged with commit SHA; coverage trend tracked in SonarQube by build.

Coverage below threshold fails the PR; a documented shortfall is allowed only via 'SDLC-Exception' ticket owned by the Engineering Manager with a 10-business-day plan to raise coverage; flaky tests quarantined and fixed within 5 days.
All changed code paths in the PR diff; verified against a mutation-testing sample on critical modules to confirm assertion strength.
Pass = all unit tests green, line coverage >=80% (>=90% critical paths), changed-line coverage >=80%; fail = any red test or coverage below threshold on changed code.
Failing tests block merge; coverage shortfall blocks merge unless waived via 'SDLC-Exception' ticket owned by the Engineering Manager; flaky specs labeled 'flaky' with a 5-business-day fix SLA.
Acceptance = new/changed public methods covered, suite green, and coverage thresholds met on changed lines, verified by the CI coverage gate and PR review.
Coverage report + test results attached to the PR check and archived in the CI system; coverage badge/trend visible in SonarQube for the repo.

All new/changed integration points for the component under delivery: REST/gRPC clients, Kafka producer/consumer bindings, and DB connections declared in the service's dependency manifest (build.gradle/pom.xml/package.json) and its OpenAPI 3.0 spec. Scope excludes third-party SaaS webhooks handled by MuleSoft.
The active development sprint (2-week cadence) in which the integration branch is opened through the release cut; integration wiring must be merged before the PI increment code-freeze date.

Every downstream endpoint has a configured base URL, timeout, and retry/circuit-breaker policy externalized to config (no hardcoded hosts); all required request/response fields validated against the consumer-driven contract in the schema registry with 0 unresolved contract-test failures.
Integration smoke test asserts request count in = response count out across each wired dependency in the staging environment; reconcile message offsets for Kafka consumers to 0 lag before promotion.
CI pipeline run URL, commit SHA, and integration-test report (JUnit XML) stored as build artifacts in the CI/CD system, retained 12 months, tagged with the Jira story key.

Failed integration or contract tests logged as Jira defects linked to the story; blocking failures gate the merge. Waiver path: Jira ticket type 'SDLC-Exception', owner = Engineering Manager, 10-business-day remediation SLA.

Integration design follows the approved solution architecture document (SAD) version referenced in the ADR; API version pinned per the twelve-month deprecation policy and recorded in the service README.
Timeout/retry sensitivity documented: p95 downstream latency budget 200ms; retries capped at 3 with exponential backoff; circuit opens at 50% error rate over a 30s window.
Materiality: any integration handling policy/claims financial transactions is treated as critical-path and requires 90% test coverage plus a load test before production.
Trace 5 sample transactions end-to-end from the calling component through each dependency to the persisted record in the target system, capturing correlation IDs at each hop.
Integration state transitions (pending/committed/failed/compensated) align to the Saga workflow defined in the SAD; verify compensating actions fire on downstream failure.
Event/record timestamps (createdAt, processedAt) are UTC and monotonic across hops; no clock-skew gaps exceeding 2s in the trace.
Contract + integration test suite executed against all wired dependencies in staging; 20 synthetic transactions covering happy path, downstream timeout, and malformed-payload cases.
PASS = 100% of contract tests green, 0 unhandled exceptions, p95 latency <= 200ms; FAIL = any contract break or unrecovered downstream error.
On FAIL, block the merge, open a Jira defect linked to the story, and route to the Integration Engineer; exception via 'SDLC-Exception' ticket, Engineering Manager approval, 10-business-day SLA.
Current sprint; tests run per pull request and again on the release-candidate build cut for the PI increment.

All regulatory, statutory, and internal-policy obligations applicable to the requested capability across data privacy (GDPR/CCPA), cybersecurity (NYDFS 500), and insurance-specific rules; scoped to the systems, data domains, and jurisdictions named in the intake request.
The requirements-elaboration phase for the current initiative; catalogue must be complete before the solution architecture document is baselined.

Each catalogued obligation records: rule citation, source regime, applicable jurisdiction, triggering data category or process, control owner, and mapped system(s); no obligation left without a named owner and a NIST CSF/ISO 27001 control mapping.
Cross-check catalogue count against the GRC platform's obligations library for the same scope; reconcile to 0 unaccounted-for in-scope obligations.
Compliance requirements register exported to the compliance evidence repository, versioned, timestamped, and linked to the Jira epic; retained per the applicable regime retention schedule.

Obligations that cannot be met in-scope logged in the regulatory filing/issue tracker with a risk rating and remediation plan; exception via 'SDLC-Exception' ticket, owner = Compliance Lead, tracked to closure.
Applicability assessment methodology follows the enterprise GRC obligations-mapping procedure, current version, recorded in the register header.
Sensitivity: any capability touching special-category or sensitive personal data escalates to a mandatory DPIA before build.
Materiality: obligations rated High (financial penalty or breach-notification exposure) require sign-off from Legal Counsel and the CISO before requirements baseline.
Each requirement cites the specific rule (e.g., 'GDPR Art. 30 RoPA', 'NYDFS 500.16 IR plan', 'CCPA 1798.100 notice at collection') and the internal policy section it maps to.
Register and supporting evidence retained per regime: GDPR/CCPA privacy records for the disclosed retention period; NYDFS cybersecurity records for a minimum of 3 years.
Any obligation with a statutory filing deadline (e.g., NYDFS annual certification by April 15) recorded with its due date and owner in the regulatory filing/issue tracker.
100% of in-scope data categories and processes assessed for applicability; sample 10 catalogued obligations for traceability back to primary regulatory text.
PASS = every in-scope obligation has citation, owner, and control mapping and reconciles to the GRC library; FAIL = any missing citation/owner or unreconciled obligation.
On FAIL, log gap in the regulatory filing/issue tracker, assign to Compliance Lead; exception via 'SDLC-Exception', 10-business-day SLA before baseline sign-off.
Acceptance = compliance register reviewed and signed by Legal Counsel; all High-rated obligations have an accepted control approach.
Register stored in the compliance evidence repository (versioned) with a link recorded on the Jira epic and the GRC platform record.

The full functional and non-functional requirement set for the requested capability, covering performance (throughput/latency), security (authN/authZ, data protection), and availability (SLA/RTO/RPO); scoped to the epic under elaboration.
Requirements-elaboration phase of the current initiative; specification baselined before the solution architecture document and sprint-0 estimation.

Every requirement is atomic, testable, and has a unique ID, priority (MoSCoW), and acceptance criteria; NFRs quantified (e.g., p95 API latency <= 200ms, 99.9% availability, RTO 4h/RPO 15m) rather than qualitative.
Requirement count in the spec reconciles to the Jira story/backlog count for the epic; 0 orphan stories without a linked requirement and 0 requirements without a story.
Requirements specification stored in Confluence with page version history; PDF snapshot at baseline attached to the Jira epic, retained 12 months.
Ambiguous or conflicting requirements logged as Jira 'clarification' sub-tasks and resolved before baseline; exception via 'SDLC-Exception', owner = Product Owner, 10-business-day SLA.
Specification uses the enterprise requirements template (current version) and INVEST criteria; NFR taxonomy references the architecture Non-Functional Requirements standard.
Sensitivity: NFR targets flagged where a 10% miss materially affects customer SLA or regulatory posture, triggering architecture review.
Materiality: Must-have security/availability NFRs require Solutions Architect and Security sign-off before the spec is baselined.
All requirements in the baselined spec (functional + NFR) reviewed in a peer walkthrough with the Solutions Architect and Test Lead.
PASS = 100% of requirements testable with acceptance criteria and all NFRs quantified; FAIL = any vague, untestable, or unquantified requirement.
On FAIL, return the requirement to the Product Owner/BA for rework; block baseline; exception via 'SDLC-Exception', 10-business-day SLA.
Data-related requirements reference field definitions from the enterprise data catalog / business glossary term links.
Where the capability reports figures, expected control totals/reconciliation targets are stated in the requirement so QA can verify.

The engineering knowledge base content: reusable patterns, Architecture Decision Records (ADRs), code samples, and lessons-learned entries owned by the engineering guild; scoped to the domains the team maintains.
Continuous, with a mandatory review at each PI boundary (quarterly); entries not touched in 12 months flagged for review or archive.
Each entry has: title, owning team, last-reviewed date, tags, and a working code sample or ADR link; ADRs follow the standard template (context/decision/consequences) and 0 entries lack an owner.
Knowledge-base entry count reconciles to the ADR index in the repo; 0 ADRs merged to main without a corresponding wiki index entry.
Confluence page version history plus git commit history for ADRs stored with code; each curation pass tagged with the PI and author, retained indefinitely as institutional record.

Stale or superseded entries marked 'deprecated' with a link to the replacement; unreviewed-past-12-months entries logged in a Jira 'KB-review' backlog. Exception via 'SDLC-Exception', owner = Tech Lead.
Curation follows the guild's documentation standard (current version); ADRs required for significant decisions and stored with code.
Sensitivity: code samples referencing security patterns reviewed by a Security Champion before publication to avoid propagating insecure examples.
Materiality: ADRs affecting cross-team architecture require ARB acknowledgement before being marked authoritative.
All KB entries modified in the current PI, plus a random sample of 10 existing entries for freshness/accuracy.
PASS = every sampled entry has an owner, a last-reviewed date within 12 months, and working links/samples; FAIL = broken sample, missing owner, or stale review.
On FAIL, create a 'KB-review' Jira task assigned to the entry owner; deprecate if unmaintainable. Exception via 'SDLC-Exception', 10-business-day SLA.
Entries describing data patterns link to enterprise data catalog term definitions rather than restating field meanings.
Not a reporting task; control-total check is N/A but entry count is reconciled to the ADR/repo index per the reconcile check above.

The internal developer portal (Backstage-style) content: service catalog entries, software templates/scaffolders, tech-docs, and self-service actions; scoped to all production services owned by engineering teams onboarded to the portal.
Continuous maintenance with a monthly reconciliation against the CMDB; every new service must appear in the catalog within one sprint of first deploy.
Every catalog entry has an owning team, lifecycle state, on-call/runbook link, repo link, and tier; catalog-info.yaml validates against schema in CI; 0 services without an owner.
Portal service count reconciles to the CMDB production-service inventory within +/-0; discrepancies raised as ServiceNow tickets.
Portal config stored as code in git (GitOps); each change is a reviewed PR with commit SHA and author; deployment record retained in the CI/CD system 12 months.
Services in CMDB but missing from the portal (or vice versa) logged as ITSM tasks assigned to the owning team; exception via 'SDLC-Exception', owner = Platform Engineering Lead, 10-business-day SLA.
All catalog entries plus all self-service scaffolder templates; smoke-test one scaffolder run end-to-end per template family.
PASS = 100% of production services present with valid catalog-info.yaml and working self-service templates; FAIL = missing service, schema-invalid entry, or broken scaffolder.
On FAIL, open an ITSM task to the Platform team, roll back the bad portal PR via GitOps; exception via 'SDLC-Exception', 10-business-day SLA.
Catalog schema fields (owner, lifecycle, tier, system) defined by the portal's catalog-info.yaml specification, referenced in the contributor guide.
Reconciliation totals: portal service count vs CMDB production count, published monthly to the platform dashboard.
All incoming demand items (features, enhancements, defects, spikes) submitted for the current intake window; each triaged for business need, strategic alignment, duplication, and rough sizing.
The current intake cycle (weekly triage cadence); triage outcome recorded within 5 business days of submission.

Each demand item has: requester, business sponsor, problem statement, expected value/ROI note, strategic-objective link, and a triage decision (accept/reject/park/need-info); 0 items left in 'new' beyond the SLA.
Count of items entering triage equals count with a recorded decision by cycle end; reconcile the Jira intake board to 0 undispositioned items at cutoff.
Triage decision and rationale recorded on the Jira intake ticket with timestamp and triager; board snapshot retained 12 months for portfolio audit.
Rejected/parked items get a documented reason and, if appealed, escalate via the intake escalation path to the PMO Manager; exception via 'SDLC-Exception', owner = Product Owner.
Triage uses the approved intake scoring model (current version) with weighted criteria for value, alignment, and effort, recorded on the board.
Sensitivity: items whose value hinges on an unvalidated assumption are flagged 'need-info' rather than accepted.
Materiality: demand above the effort threshold (e.g., > 40 story points or cross-team) requires a business case and PMO review before acceptance.

Go/No-Go decision (Approved / Conditional / Rejected) documented on the Jira release and in the release readiness review minutes in Confluence, with residual-risk statement and any conditions.

Sign-off distributed to Release Manager, Product Owner, DevOps Engineer, delivery squad, and Operations/Support via the Jira release comment and the #release-readiness Teams channel; recipient list captured in the review minutes.
The complete mandatory test scope for the RC build (unit, integration, contract, regression, security, performance) — no sampling; each suite's latest run tied to the build SHA.

PASS = 0 blocker/critical defects, coverage ≥ 80% changed / ≥ 90% critical paths, 100% regression green, 0 critical/high SAST/DAST findings, performance within SLA; FAIL = any unmet gate without an approved SDLC-Exception.

On FAIL, withhold sign-off and block deployment; open an SDLC-Exception (owner = Engineering Manager) for any risk-accepted item; only an approved conditional waiver with a dated remediation plan permits release.
In-scope period = the RC build's test-execution window; effective dates = the release's target deployment date recorded on the Jira release and the ServiceNow change record.
